5.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.
5.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land

6.meaning: and in the evening / and at nightfall
6.grammar: conjunction + noun in the accusative — ʿashiyy/ʿashā means the time from late afternoon to nightfall; the -an tanwīn marks it as indefinite and in the accusative (used as a time adverb); one of the times mentioned for glorification of Allah
6.root: ع-ش-و (ʿ-sh-w) — evening, nightfall; to be in the evening

7.meaning: and when / and at the time

parts.en: when / at the time (temporal particle, accusative)

7.grammar: conjunction + temporal particle — ḥīna is a time word meaning 'when' or 'at the time of'; the accusative -a ending marks it as a time adverb; it is typically followed by a verb or verbal clause specifying the time

8.meaning: you are at noon / you enter the midday time

parts.en: you enter the noon time (2nd person masculine plural imperfect)

8.grammar: verb, active voice, imperfect tense (Form IV), 2nd person masculine plural — from aẓhara 'to enter the noon (ẓuhr) time'; the tu- prefix marks 2nd person; -ūna marks the masculine plural indicative; refers to the midday hour, when ẓuhr prayer is performed
8.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — noon, midday; back; to be at noon (Form IV)

1.meaning: To bring out, produce, or cause to come forth — to make something emerge from where it was hidden or contained. The causative pattern means 'to make (something) go out'.

parts.en: brings forth / causes to come out

1.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular of the causative pattern: 'he/it brings forth'. The 'yu-' prefix marks 'he/it' and the causative vowel pattern adds the sense 'causes to come out'. The final '-u' marks the ongoing (indicative) mood — an action happening or habitual.

2.meaning: The living — that which is alive, possessing life and vitality.
2.grammar: A definite noun/adjective ('al-' = 'the'). Because the following letter 'ḥ' is a 'moon letter,' the 'l' of 'al-' is fully pronounced and does NOT assimilate (al-ḥayy). The final '-a' is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
2.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life, being alive

3.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
3.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

4.meaning: The dead — that which is lifeless, having lost or never possessed life.
4.grammar: A definite noun/adjective on the intensive pattern 'fayʿil' ('al-' = 'the,' its 'l' assimilated into the following 'm'). The final '-i' is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding noun ('… OF the dead') or as following a preposition or governing particle.

5.meaning: And He brings out / brings forth — the same act of producing something out of another, prefixed with 'and.'
5.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and.' The verb is present-tense Form IV (causative): yu- marks a 'he/it' subject, and the form means 'cause to emerge.' The final -u is the normal present-tense ending, conveying ongoing or habitual bringing-forth.
5.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, emerge; (causative) bring out

6.meaning: The dead — that which is lifeless, having lost or never possessed life.
6.grammar: A definite noun/adjective on the intensive pattern 'fayʿil' ('al-' = 'the,' its 'l' assimilated into the following 'm'). The final '-a' is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

7.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
7.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

8.meaning: The living; that which has life, is alive and vital. Used as an adjective/noun for a living thing as opposed to the dead.
8.grammar: A definite noun/adjective with the article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive case, governed here by a possessive construct (iḍāfa): it is the second term following the active participle 'bringer-forth', giving 'bringer-forth OF the living'. The genitive is not from a preposition but from this possessive linkage.

9.meaning: and He gives life / and He revives
9.grammar: conjunction + verb, active voice, imperfect tense (Form IV), 3rd person masculine singular — from aḥyā 'to give life, revive'; the verb ends in a weak letter (yāʾ); the subject is Allah; Form IV of ḥayiya means 'to cause to live'
9.root: ح-ي-و/ي (ḥ-y-w/y) — life; to live; Form IV: to give life

10.meaning: 'the earth,' 'the ground,' 'the land' — the earth as a whole, or the land/ground beneath us. It denotes the terrestrial expanse on which creatures live and walk.
10.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case) — the role of the thing acted upon, e.g. the direct object of a verb. The prefixed 'al-' makes it definite, 'the earth.'

11.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
11.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
11.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

12.meaning: Its death, its lifelessness or dormancy; the state of being dead, joined to a possessor.
12.grammar: A noun ('death') with an attached third-person feminine singular possessive pronoun ('its / her'). The -i vowel on the noun is genitive, the case taken before a possessor pronoun and after prepositions ('death of it').

13.meaning: 'And likewise / and in the same way / and thus' — a connective phrase pointing back to a manner just mentioned and saying 'in that very way…'. Built from 'and' + 'like' + 'that'.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; the prefix ka- means 'like/as'; 'dhālika' is the demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or already mentioned). Because ka- acts like a preposition, the word after it stands in the genitive, though the demonstrative 'dhālika' keeps a fixed form and shows no visible case change. The whole means 'and just like that / and thus'.

14.meaning: 'You (all) are brought out / brought forth' — to be taken or made to emerge from somewhere, said of a group being addressed, in the passive voice.
14.grammar: A passive present-tense verb (causative pattern 'akhraja' = to bring out). The vowel pattern 'tu-...-a-' marks the passive: the subject does not act but is acted upon ('you are brought out' rather than 'you bring out'). The 'tu-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural addressee and the indicative mood (ongoing/future).

1.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
1.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

2.meaning: 'His signs / His verses.' The plural of a word meaning a sign, token, or mark that points to a greater reality — also used for the verses of revelation — here joined to 'his'.
2.grammar: A sound feminine plural ('signs') with an attached possessive 'his'. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form this plural takes when it follows a preposition or is linked as the object of a possessor; the -hi ('his') marks ownership: 'his signs'.
2.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark; a verse of revelation

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: 'He created you' — He brought you into existence, originating and shaping you. The verb denotes bringing something into being and giving it its form and proportion, here with 'you (plural)' as the one(s) created.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb with an attached object pronoun. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer in the completed past ('he created'). The suffix '-kum' is the object 'you (plural),' i.e. the ones to whom the action was done.

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: 'Dust / earth / soil.' The noun turāb denotes dust or dry earth — the fine soil of the ground.
6.grammar: A masculine noun. The -in ending marks it as indefinite ('dust / some dust') and in the genitive case — the form used after a preposition (e.g., 'from …') or when linked to a preceding noun.

7.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
7.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

8.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

9.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
9.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

10.meaning: 'A human being, a mortal man' — bashar denotes humankind as flesh-and-blood mortals. It emphasizes the human, bodily nature of a person.
10.grammar: A noun (also usable collectively for 'mankind'). The -un ending is nominative with tanwīn (nunation — the doubled 'n' sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a human being'). The nominative case marks it as the subject of a sentence (e.g. the one who acts) or as a noun whose existence is being affirmed or denied.

11.meaning: you disperse / you spread out

parts.en: you spread out / disperse (2nd person masculine plural imperfect)

11.grammar: verb, active voice, imperfect tense (Form VIII), 2nd person masculine plural — from intashara 'to spread out, disperse, scatter'; the -ta- infix marks Form VIII (reflexive); tu- prefix marks 2nd person; -ūna marks the masculine plural indicative
11.root: ن-ش-ر (n-sh-r) — to spread, scatter, publish

1.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
1.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

2.meaning: 'His signs / His verses.' The plural of a word meaning a sign, token, or mark that points to a greater reality — also used for the verses of revelation — here joined to 'his'.
2.grammar: A sound feminine plural ('signs') with an attached possessive 'his'. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form this plural takes when it follows a preposition or is linked as the object of a possessor; the -hi ('his') marks ownership: 'his signs'.
2.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark; a verse of revelation

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: 'He created' — to bring into being, to originate and shape something that did not exist before, from the root denoting creation and the fashioning of things from nothing.
4.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'), completed action ('he created'). This is a form I verb of the CaCaCa pattern. The masculine singular 'he' here is the unmarked (zero-suffix) form — there is no separate person ending; the final -a is the inherent stem vowel of the base pattern, not a person or tense suffix.

5.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

7.meaning: 'Yourselves' — literally 'your own selves/souls.' Anfus is the plural of nafs ('self, soul, person'); with the attached pronoun it expresses the reflexive 'your own selves.'
7.grammar: A plural noun ('selves') with an attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your,' masculine plural). The -i ending is genitive: the noun is governed by a preceding preposition or stands in a possessive ('of …') construction.

8.meaning: A noun meaning 'spouses', 'mates', or 'wives' — the plural of a word denoting one of a pair joined together, hence a husband or wife. Context determines whether husbands or wives are meant.
8.grammar: A plural noun with the -an ending, which is accusative and indefinite. The accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The azC-ā-C shape is a broken-plural pattern. The singular denotes either partner of a married pair.
8.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — to pair, to join as a couple; spouse, mate

9.meaning: so that you may find rest / so that you may seek tranquility

parts.en: so that / in order to (lam of purpose)

9.grammar: lam of purpose + verb in subjunctive (Form I), 2nd person masculine plural — li- introduces the purpose clause; taskunū is the subjunctive form (no -na ending) of sakana 'to be still, rest, dwell'; the root means both to settle/dwell and to find stillness/rest
9.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to be still, dwell, find rest

10.meaning: Toward it / to her — the directional preposition 'ilā' ('to, toward'), expressing motion or inclination toward a goal, here joined to a feminine 'it/her'.
10.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to/toward', whose form shifts from 'ilā' to 'ilay-' when a pronoun attaches. The suffix -hā is the feminine singular object ('it/her'). It marks the endpoint or direction of motion or leaning.

11.meaning: 'And he made / appointed / rendered' — the connector 'and' joined to a past-tense verb meaning to make something into something, to fashion or appoint it. It can mean to create, to assign, or to cause a thing to become a certain way.
11.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a past-tense (perfect) verb. The bare verb with its final -a vowel denotes a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he made/did').
11.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

12.meaning: Between you / among you; the space or relation linking the members of a group.
12.grammar: An adverb of place ('between/among') with an attached pronoun. The fixed -a ending is characteristic of such place-words; the ending -kum means 'you' for a group, so the whole means 'among you all'.
12.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation/interval; the space between two things

13.meaning: A noun meaning 'affection, love, fond attachment' — warm goodwill and tender liking between people.
13.grammar: A feminine verbal noun on the pattern mafʿala. The -an ending (with tanwīn on the tā' marbūṭa, hence -tan) is the indefinite accusative: it typically marks the noun as an object of a verb, or as a specifying complement ('… in respect of …').
13.root: و-د-د (w-d-d) — love, affection, fond attachment

14.meaning: 'Mercy' — compassion and loving kindness shown by bestowing good and relieving hardship. From the same root as 'womb,' it carries a sense of nurturing tenderness.
14.grammar: A feminine singular noun ending in tāʾ marbūṭa (ة), an integral letter of the word. The tanwīn fatḥ on that ة (-tan) marks it as indefinite and accusative — the case of a direct object or of something granted. The wa- prefix means 'and'; the shadda written on وَّ reflects a recitation convention (idghām at the junction with the preceding word), not an assimilation of the conjunction itself.

15.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
15.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

16.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
16.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

17.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
17.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

18.meaning: Surely signs, tokens, or clear indications; evidences that point to a greater truth. The prefixed lām adds emphasis ('surely / indeed').
18.grammar: An emphatic particle 'la-' ('surely') joined to an indefinite feminine plural noun ('signs'). The -āt- is the sound feminine plural marker; the final -in (nunation) marks it indefinite. For this plural pattern the -in form serves for both the accusative and the genitive case.

19.meaning: For a people, for a folk or community; a group of human beings considered together. Joined to the preposition 'li' ('for / to').
19.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for / to') plus an indefinite singular noun ('a people'). The -in ending (nunation) marks indefiniteness; it is the genitive form, required because nouns governed by 'li' stand in the genitive.
19.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

20.meaning: 'They reflect / ponder / think deeply / contemplate' — a verb for sustained, careful mental consideration and turning a matter over in the mind.
20.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb in an intensive/reflexive pattern conveying deliberate, repeated reflection. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the -ūna ending indicates the indicative mood (a plain factual statement).

3.meaning: the creation / the act of creating
3.grammar: verbal noun (maṣdar), masculine, definite or in construct, nominative — the -u ending marks the nominative; khalq is the masdar of khalaqa 'to create'; it refers both to the act of creation and to the created thing; when in construct before a genitive it means 'the creation of'

4.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
4.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

5.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
5.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.
5.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land

6.meaning: and the diversity / and the difference / and the variation
6.grammar: conjunction + verbal noun (Form VIII), nominative — ikhtilāf is the masdar of ikhtalapha 'to differ, vary'; the -u ending marks the nominative; in construct before a genitive noun it means 'the diversity/variation of'; Form VIII adds the reflexive meaning of things differing from each other
6.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to differ, come after, succeed; Form VIII: to vary

7.meaning: your languages / your tongues
7.grammar: broken plural noun in construct (iḍāfa), genitive + possessive pronoun — alsinah is the broken plural of lisān 'tongue/language'; the -i of the construct genitive + -kum (2nd person masculine plural possessive) means 'your tongues/languages'

8.meaning: and your colors / and your hues
8.grammar: conjunction + broken plural in iḍāfa, genitive — alwān is the broken plural of lawn 'color'; the -i marks the genitive (governed by the preceding conjunction structure); -kum is the possessive; refers to the diversity of human skin tones and appearances

13.meaning: for those of knowledge / for the people who know
13.grammar: preposition + definite active participle (Form I), masculine plural — li- is a preposition meaning 'for'; al-ʿālimīna is the sound masculine plural (accusative/genitive form, -īna) of ʿālim 'one who knows'; used for scholars, those possessing knowledge; indicates who benefits from the sign
13.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; ʿālim: one who knows

3.meaning: your sleep / your slumber
3.grammar: noun of place/time (mīm pattern) in construct + possessive — manām is the mīm-pattern masdar/noun meaning 'sleep' or 'the sleeping place'; the -u marks nominative; -kum is the 2nd person masculine plural possessive; mentioned as one of the signs of Allah
3.root: ن-و-م (n-w-m) — to sleep; manām: sleep / place of sleep

4.meaning: By night / in the nighttime — the preposition 'in/by' joined to 'the night,' the dark portion of the day; expressing the time during which something occurs.
4.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, by') on the noun 'the night' (with the definite article al-, its l- assimilated into the following letter). The preposition forces the genitive case, shown by the final -i. Here the phrase marks the time when something takes place.

5.meaning: And the day / daytime — the period of light from dawn to sunset.
5.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and'; 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'n', said an-nahār). A noun for the daylight hours. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the day').
5.root: ن-ه-ر (n-h-r) — daylight; (also) river, flowing

6.meaning: and your seeking / and your striving (for livelihood)
6.grammar: conjunction + verbal noun (Form VIII) in construct + possessive — ibtighāʾ is the masdar of ibtaighā 'to seek, strive for'; Form VIII adds intensity; the -u marks nominative; -kum is possessive; refers to seeking one's livelihood or sustenance
6.root: ب-غ-و/ي (b-gh-w/y) — to seek, desire; Form VIII: to strive to seek

8.meaning: 'His bounty / grace / favor' — faḍl is overflowing generosity, an extra goodness given beyond what is owed; with the attached pronoun it means the bounty belonging to Him (Allah).
8.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the noun to what follows in an 'of' relationship; here it carries through to the possessor.
8.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus; hence bounty, grace, superiority

13.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

14.meaning: 'They hear / listen' — a present-tense verb for hearing sounds, and by extension listening or heeding.
14.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' hearing now or habitually. The full -ūna ending shows the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state.

1.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

2.meaning: 'His signs / His verses.' The plural of a word meaning a sign, token, or mark that points to a greater reality — also used for the verses of revelation — here joined to 'his'.
2.grammar: A sound feminine plural ('signs') with an attached possessive 'his'. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form this plural takes when it follows a preposition or is linked as the object of a possessor; the -hi ('his') marks ownership: 'his signs'.
2.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark; a verse of revelation

3.meaning: A verb-plus-object meaning 'he shows you / causes you to see' — to make a group of addressees behold or perceive something.
3.grammar: A present-tense (Form IV, causative) verb: 'he makes (you) see, he shows.' The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject. The attached -kum means 'you all' (the ones shown); its vowel appears as -kumu to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting (hamzat-waṣl) alif.

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'the lightning' — the bright flash that appears in storm clouds.
4.grammar: A noun made definite by al- ('the'). The final -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb — the thing being acted upon.

5.meaning: Fear, dread, apprehension — the inner state of being afraid of harm or of an outcome. As an indefinite noun it can also function adverbially: "out of fear, fearfully."
5.grammar: An indefinite masculine singular noun in the accusative case. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ("a fear") and accusative, a case often used to express the manner or reason of an action ("in/out of fear").
5.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — to fear, be afraid, dread

6.meaning: Avid desire, coveting, craving — the acquisitive eagerness for something one wants to obtain. Intrinsically the word carries a sense of greedy or grasping want; in many contexts it is rendered as eager hope or longing for some good, but its core nuance is covetous desire rather than neutral, noble hope (which is rajāʾ/amal). As an indefinite noun it can work adverbially: "in eager desire, hopefully."
6.grammar: Conjunction "and" + an indefinite masculine singular noun in the accusative case. The -an (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and accusative, a case often expressing the manner or reason of an action ("in/out of eager desire").
6.root: ط-م-ع (ṭ-m-ʿ) — to covet, crave, eagerly desire, be greedy for

7.meaning: and He sends down / and He causes to descend
7.grammar: conjunction + verb, active voice, imperfect tense (Form II), 3rd person masculine singular — Form II (nazzala) adds intensity/frequency to nazala 'to descend'; yunazzilu means He sends down repeatedly or in stages; the -u ending marks the indicative
7.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; Form II: to send down

8.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
8.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

9.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
9.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
9.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; sky, heaven

10.meaning: 'water' — water in general, the fluid essential to life; also used for liquid such as rain. A basic noun for the substance of water.
10.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks the accusative case together with indefiniteness — commonly the role of a direct object, the thing acted upon (e.g. what is sent down or brought).

11.meaning: and gives life / and so He revives (the earth)
11.grammar: consequence particle + verb (Form IV), 3rd person masculine singular — fa- indicates result or sequence; yuḥyī is Form IV of ḥayiya 'to cause to live'; ends in a weak yāʾ; the subject is Allah; refers to reviving the dead earth after rainfall
11.root: ح-ي-و/ي (ḥ-y-w/y) — life; Form IV: to give life

12.meaning: By it, with it, through it; the preposition 'bi' (with/by means of) joined to a pronoun referring to something previously mentioned.
12.grammar: A preposition plus an attached third-person masculine singular pronoun ('it / him'). 'Bi' conveys instrument or means ('by means of it'); the pronoun takes the -i vowel because words governed by 'bi' stand in the genitive.

13.meaning: 'the earth,' 'the ground,' 'the land' — the earth as a whole, or the land/ground beneath us. It denotes the terrestrial expanse on which creatures live and walk.
13.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case) — the role of the thing acted upon, e.g. the direct object of a verb. The prefixed 'al-' makes it definite, 'the earth.'
13.root: أ-ر-ض (ʼ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

14.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
14.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
14.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

15.meaning: Its death, its lifelessness or dormancy; the state of being dead, joined to a possessor.
15.grammar: A noun ('death') with an attached third-person feminine singular possessive pronoun ('its / her'). The -i vowel on the noun is genitive, the case taken before a possessor pronoun and after prepositions ('death of it').

16.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
16.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

17.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
17.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

18.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
18.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

19.meaning: Surely signs, tokens, or clear indications; evidences that point to a greater truth. The prefixed lām adds emphasis ('surely / indeed').
19.grammar: An emphatic particle 'la-' ('surely') joined to an indefinite feminine plural noun ('signs'). The -āt- is the sound feminine plural marker; the final -in (nunation) marks it indefinite. For this plural pattern the -in form serves for both the accusative and the genitive case.

20.meaning: For a people, for a folk or community; a group of human beings considered together. Joined to the preposition 'li' ('for / to').
20.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for / to') plus an indefinite singular noun ('a people'). The -in ending (nunation) marks indefiniteness; it is the genitive form, required because nouns governed by 'li' stand in the genitive.
20.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

21.meaning: They use their reason, they understand and reflect; to grasp things with the intellect and restrain oneself accordingly.
21.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The -na ending also signals the indicative mood, used for a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action ('they use reason').
21.root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l) — to reason, understand; to restrain (as a tether restrains)

1.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
1.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

2.meaning: 'His signs / His verses.' The plural of a word meaning a sign, token, or mark that points to a greater reality — also used for the verses of revelation — here joined to 'his'.
2.grammar: A sound feminine plural ('signs') with an attached possessive 'his'. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form this plural takes when it follows a preposition or is linked as the object of a possessor; the -hi ('his') marks ownership: 'his signs'.
2.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark; a verse of revelation

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: "That you stand / you should stand" — to rise and stand upright; can also carry the sense of taking a standing position for worship. Addressed to one male in a softened, non-final mood.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ta- prefix meaning "you" (one male). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which appears after certain particles (such as "that / so that / to") and gives the sense of a possible, intended, or purposed action rather than a plain statement of fact.

5.meaning: The sky / the heaven — the canopy overhead, the firmament; whatever rises above and overarches. The root sense is height and that which is elevated above.
5.grammar: A noun made definite by the prefixed al- ('the'). The -u ending signals the nominative case — the form typically used when the noun is the subject of a sentence (the one doing or undergoing the action). The word is grammatically feminine.
5.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness, that which is elevated

6.meaning: 'and the earth' — the ground, land, and world beneath, as opposed to the heavens. The leading 'wa' joins it ('and …') and the definite article marks it as the known earth.
6.grammar: A definite feminine noun joined by 'wa' ('and'). The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as the subject or topic of a sentence ('and the earth [is …]').

7.meaning: With/by His command — amr means a command, order, decree, or matter/affair; with the preposition bi- ('with, by') and the pronoun 'His' it conveys 'by His command' or 'by His decree'.
7.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with' or 'by'. The noun amr takes the genitive -i ending (required after the preposition bi-) and then the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The genitive marks the noun as governed by the preposition.
7.root: ء-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command, order; a matter/affair

8.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
8.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

9.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.
9.root: — (a time particle; no triliteral root)

10.meaning: He called you (plural), summoned you, invited you. From a root meaning 'to call / summon / invite / pray,' the verb denotes calling out to someone, with the attached object 'you all.'
10.grammar: A past-tense verb with an attached object pronoun. The base daʿā is third-person masculine singular past ('he called'), its final weak letter appearing as a long ā. The suffix -kum is the object 'you all,' addressing a group.
10.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, supplicate

11.meaning: a single call / one summons
11.grammar: verbal noun, feminine, indefinite, accusative — daʿwa is the noun of action from daʿā 'to call, invite, summon'; the -tan tanwīn marks it as indefinite accusative; in the context of the Resurrection, it refers to the single divine call that will raise the dead
11.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, invite, summon

12.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
12.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

13.meaning: the earth / the ground / the land
13.grammar: noun, feminine, definite, genitive — al-arḍ is 'the earth' or 'the ground'; the -i ending marks the genitive case (governed by a preposition or in construct); arḍ is feminine in Arabic and used for the entire earth or a specific land
13.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, ground, land

14.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
14.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

15.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
15.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

16.meaning: you will come forth / you will emerge

parts.en: you come forth / emerge (2nd person masculine plural imperfect)

16.grammar: verb, active voice, imperfect tense (Form I), 2nd person masculine plural — from kharaja 'to go out, emerge'; the ta- prefix marks 2nd person; -ūna marks masculine plural indicative; in the context of the Resurrection, it means coming forth from the graves
16.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit, emerge

1.meaning: And for him / and he has — the connector 'and', the preposition 'for/to', and the pronoun 'him'. Together it expresses possession or belonging ('and to him belongs …', 'and he has …').
1.grammar: A small phrase, not a verb: the connector wa- ('and') + the preposition la- ('for/to') + the pronoun -hu ('him'). The preposition with a pronoun commonly conveys having or belonging ('he has', 'belonging to him').

2.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
2.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
2.root: — (pronoun)

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
4.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

5.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
5.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.
5.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'all,' 'each,' 'every,' or 'the whole.' It denotes totality — that the entirety of a group or thing is included.
6.grammar: A noun in the nominative case with 'tanwīn' (the -un ending), which marks it as indefinite and as the subject or doer of a sentence. Standing alone with tanwīn it carries the sense 'everyone / all of them' as an independent subject.

7.meaning: A two-part phrase 'for Him' or 'to Him belongs,' expressing possession, ownership, or that something is due to one masculine being.
7.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to/belonging to') with its vowel shifted to 'la-' before the pronoun. The attached -hu means 'Him', so the whole means 'for Him' or 'His'; the preposition signals possession or that something is owed or directed to that person.

8.meaning: devoutly obedient / humbly submissive
8.grammar: active participle (Form I), masculine plural, nominative — qānit means one who is devoutly obedient and humbly submissive, especially in prayer; the -ūna ending marks masculine plural nominative; the root qanata means to be obedient/humble
8.root: ق-ن-ت (q-n-t) — to be devoutly obedient, humble before Allah

1.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: To begin, originate, or bring something into being for the first time — to start an action or initiate creation from nothing.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he begins/originates'). The 'ya-' prefix marks the present tense with a 'he' subject. The final '-u' is the plain indicative ending used for ongoing or habitual action. It normally takes an object — the thing being initiated.

4.meaning: The creation — the act of bringing things into existence, and by extension all that is created; the created order brought forth by Allah.
4.grammar: A singular noun made definite by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative case, which most often identifies the direct object of a verb ('originates the creation').

5.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
5.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

6.meaning: To repeat, restore, or bring back — to return something to a former state, do it over again, or reproduce it. With the attached pronoun: 'He repeats/restores it'.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he restores'), from a verb-form that makes the action transitive ('to bring something back'). The 'yu-' prefix marks the present tense with a 'he' subject. The '-u' before the pronoun is the indicative ending (ongoing/habitual action); the attached '-hu' is the object pronoun 'it/him'.

7.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
7.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

8.meaning: easier / simpler / more manageable
8.grammar: elative (comparative/superlative) adjective, masculine singular, nominative — from the root hawana 'to be easy, light, insignificant'; the -u ending marks nominative; ahwanu means 'easier' or 'less significant'; used to express that the second creation (resurrection) is no harder than the first
8.root: ه-و-ن (h-w-n) — to be easy, light, insignificant

9.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
9.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

10.meaning: 'And for Him / and to Him belongs' — the preposition 'for/to' expressing belonging or possession, joined with the pronoun 'Him.' It conveys that something belongs or is due to Him.
10.grammar: A small phrase: the connector 'and' plus the preposition la- ('for, to, belonging to') with the attached pronoun -hu ('Him'). The construction 'la- + pronoun' expresses possession or entitlement — 'and to Him belongs …' / 'and for Him is …'

11.meaning: The likeness, example, comparison, or parable — a description by way of resemblance, or a standard held up to illustrate something.
11.grammar: A definite noun ('the likeness'). The '-u' ending is nominative, the case a noun typically carries when it is the subject of a sentence ('the likeness is …').
11.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similitude, example

12.meaning: The highest, the most exalted, the loftiest — the superlative 'highest/most high.'
12.grammar: A definite superlative adjective ('the highest'). It is of the 'af'al' superlative pattern and ends in a fixed long '-ā' (its last root letter being a weak vowel), so its ending does not change for case.
12.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — height, loftiness, to be high/exalted

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
13.root: — (particle)

14.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
14.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

15.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
15.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

16.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
16.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

17.meaning: "the All-Mighty / the Ever-Dominant" — one who is mighty, invincible, and held in honour; as a divine name 'al-ʿAzīz' denotes the One who is supremely powerful, unconquerable, and exalted above all.
17.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong, enduring quality. The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

18.meaning: "the All-Wise" — one full of wisdom, who judges and orders everything with perfect, sound judgement; as a divine name 'al-Ḥakīm' denotes the One whose every act and decree is supremely wise.
18.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, abiding quality ('ever-wise'). The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form a word takes as the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description.
18.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, govern; wisdom

1.meaning: He struck / set forth — literally 'to hit', but commonly used in the sense of putting forward or coining a likeness or example.
1.grammar: Past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), shown by the bare stem with its final -a. So: 'he struck' or 'he set forth (an example)'.
1.root: ض-ر-ب (ḍ-r-b) — to strike, hit; to set forth, coin (a likeness)

2.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
2.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

3.meaning: A likeness, comparison, parable, or illustrative example — a similitude held up so that an abstract truth can be grasped through a concrete picture.
3.grammar: A noun. The -an ending is accusative with nunation (the doubled 'n' sound), the case typically marking the direct object of a verb — the thing acted upon ('an example').

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: 'Yourselves' — literally 'your own selves/souls.' Anfus is the plural of nafs ('self, soul, person'); with the attached pronoun it expresses the reflexive 'your own selves.'
5.grammar: A plural noun ('selves') with an attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your,' masculine plural). The -i ending is genitive: the noun is governed by a preceding preposition or stands in a possessive ('of …') construction.
5.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self / soul / breath

6.meaning: is there? / have they? (interrogative particle)
6.grammar: interrogative particle — hal is used to introduce yes/no questions in Arabic; it does not carry case; it often implies the expected answer is 'no' in rhetorical questions (hal min shufaʿāʾ = 'are there any intercessors?' — expecting 'no')

7.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
7.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

9.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
9.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
9.root: — (particle; no root)

10.meaning: It/she possessed, owned, or held in ownership — a completed act of having something under one's control or right.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb with the feminine ending -at: 'she/it possessed'. The -at marks completed action by a feminine singular subject. In the idiom 'what your right hands have possessed', the feminine subject is the (grammatically feminine) 'right hands'.
10.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, possess, hold sway

11.meaning: Your (plural) right hands — literally the right hands, used idiomatically for solemn oaths and for lawful possession or authority. With the suffix: 'your right hands'.
11.grammar: A plural noun carrying the nominative -u ending, which typically marks it as the subject (the doer) of a verb. The suffix -kum is the attached possessive pronoun 'your' (plural masculine). The plural can mean 'right hands' or 'oaths', and the phrase 'what your right hands possess' is an idiom for those under one's lawful charge.
11.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand/side; oath; good fortune

12.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
12.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

13.meaning: Associates, partners, or co-sharers — those set up as participants alongside another in ownership, authority, or worship. In theological usage it denotes rivals falsely placed beside Allah.
13.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of sharīk ('partner'), following the pattern faʿalāʾ. This pattern is a diptote, so it takes no nunation. The word is in the accusative case, marked by the short -a vowel on the word-final hamzah (آءَ); that hamzah is part of the plural pattern itself and cannot be split off as a separate ending. The accusative is the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('they made/claimed partners') or after certain particles.
13.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partake, associate

14.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
14.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

15.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
15.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

16.meaning: 'We provided you' / 'we granted you sustenance' — to bestow provision, livelihood, or sustenance upon someone. Marked for a 'we' subject acting upon 'you (plural)'.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb carrying two attached pronouns. The first suffix -nā marks the doer, 'we'; the second suffix -kum marks the receiver, 'you (plural)'. So the form means 'we provided you'. The verb denotes granting provision or sustenance.

17.grammar: connective particle + independent personal pronoun — fa- links to the preceding context; antum is the independent 2nd person masculine plural pronoun; used for emphasis of the subject; the combination fa-antum often introduces a result or rhetorical question

18.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
18.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

19.meaning: 'Equal / the same / all alike' — a noun-adjective expressing that two or more things make no difference and are on a par. It often appears in the sense 'it is all the same (whether… or…)'.
19.grammar: A singular indefinite noun used to mean 'equal/the same'. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a/an…') and in the nominative case — the case used for the subject or for the predicate that describes what something is.
19.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — to be even, equal, level

20.meaning: you fear them / you are afraid of them

parts.en: you fear (2nd person masculine plural imperfect)

20.grammar: verb (imperfect, Form I) + object pronoun — takhāfūna is 2nd person masculine plural of khāfa 'to fear'; -ūna marks the indicative; -hum is the 3rd person masculine plural object pronoun; the question 'do you fear them as you fear Allah?' is rhetorical

21.meaning: as you fear (Him) / like your fear (of Allah)
21.grammar: preposition of comparison + noun in construct + possessive — ka- means 'as/like'; khīfat is a noun of manner from khāfa 'to fear' (like a noun of quality); the -i marks the construct genitive; -kum is the possessive; together: 'like your fear (of Allah)'
21.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — to fear; khīfa: fear, awe

22.meaning: 'Yourselves' — your own selves, persons, or souls. The base noun 'nafs' means the self, soul, or inner person.
22.grammar: A plural noun, 'selves,' with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('your,' addressed to a group). The '-a' before the pronoun is the accusative case, marking the word as the direct object — the thing being acted upon.

23.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
23.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
23.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

24.meaning: 'We set out in detail / expound clearly' — to distinguish a thing part by part, laying it out distinctly and explaining it in full detail.
24.grammar: A present-tense verb of the intensive (form II) pattern, which adds the sense of doing something thoroughly or part by part. The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain ongoing or habitual action ('we expound in detail').
24.root: ف-ص-ل (f-ṣ-l) — separating, distinguishing, setting apart in detail

25.meaning: 'The signs / the verses' — the plural of 'sign,' referring to clear indicators, proofs, miracles, or the verses of revelation that point to truth.
25.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the signs'), made definite by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The sound feminine plural takes the -i ending when it is an object of a verb or linked after a preposition or possessor — that is, when it is grammatically governed rather than serving as the subject.

26.meaning: 'For a people / for a folk' — directed toward a community or group of human beings considered collectively.
26.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a noun 'people.' Because it follows a preposition, the noun takes the genitive, and the tanwīn (the -in ending) marks it as indefinite ('a people'). The whole phrase means 'for a people,' directing something toward that group.
26.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

27.meaning: They use their reason, they understand and reflect; to grasp things with the intellect and restrain oneself accordingly.
27.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The -na ending also signals the indicative mood, used for a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action ('they use reason').
27.root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l) — to reason, understand; to restrain (as a tether restrains)

1.meaning: Rather / nay, but — a particle that cancels or corrects what came before and introduces a contrasting truth: 'no — instead …'. It sets aside a prior idea and replaces it.
1.grammar: A particle of retraction and correction; it does not change endings on other words. Its base form is 'bal'; the final -i here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word that begins with a cluster.

2.meaning: Means 'he followed / pursued' — to go after something and adopt it, walking in its path or seeking it out, whether following a person, a way, or an aim.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with a built-in doer 'he' (a single male): 'he followed.' It is built on the reflexive ift'aʿala pattern (which inserts a -t- after the first root letter); this pattern adds the sense of actively pursuing or making something one's own. Here the first root letter ت merges with that inserted -t-, producing the doubled ت heard at the start (it-ta-) — so the doubling is at the front from this merging, not in the middle root letter. The final -a is the standard past-tense ending.
2.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
4.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

5.meaning: Their desires, inclinations, cravings; the pulls of personal whim and passion — what one leans toward apart from guidance, here belonging to 'them'.
5.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of hawā ('desire, inclination, whim'). The case-vowel -a (accusative) typically marks the object of a verb. The attached pronoun -hum means 'their' (a group of males or mixed). Altogether: 'their desires/whims'.
5.root: ه-و-ي (h-w-y) — inclination, desire, whim; to incline toward, to fall

6.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
6.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
6.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

7.meaning: 'Knowledge.' A noun denoting sure, established knowing — to know a thing as it truly is. In its indefinite form it often appears in the sense 'any knowledge (at all).'
7.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('any knowledge'). The genitive -i is the form used after a preposition such as 'of' or 'by' — e.g. 'of any knowledge.'

8.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
8.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

9.meaning: 'He/it guides, leads, shows the way'. The verb means to direct someone toward a goal or along a right path — to lead aright.
9.grammar: A third-person masculine singular present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a 'he/it' subject, and the final long -ī carries the sense 'he guides'. (This verb takes an object directly, 'guides someone', without needing 'to'.)
9.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead aright, show the way

10.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
10.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

11.meaning: He let go astray / led astray, or he went astray — to cause someone to lose the right way, or to stray from it oneself.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he …'), in the causative pattern ('to cause to go astray'). The final -a (with the doubled lām) is the past-tense singular marker.
11.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
12.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

13.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
13.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
13.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

14.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
14.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

15.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
15.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

16.meaning: Helpers / supporters: those who give aid, support, and victory to another, standing by them against an adversary; the plural of 'helper'.
16.grammar: A masculine plural active participle — a 'doer' word meaning 'ones who help'. The sound plural ending -īna marks more than two; this -īna form (rather than -ūna) is the case used for objects of verbs and after prepositions or in possession (the accusative/genitive).
16.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to give victory/support

1.meaning: so set / so establish / so direct (your face)
1.grammar: connective particle + imperative verb (Form IV), 2nd person masculine singular — fa- introduces the consequential command; aqim is the imperative of aqāma (Form IV of qāma) 'to establish, set upright'; when used with wajhaka ('your face') it means to set/direct oneself firmly
1.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand; Form IV: to establish, set upright

2.meaning: Your face; the front of the head — and by extension one's countenance or direction. Addressed to a single male ('your'), and here the object of an action.
2.grammar: The noun 'face' (wajh) with the attached pronoun -ka ('your', for one male). The -a ending before the pronoun is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('turn … your face').
2.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, that which one faces

3.meaning: To / for the religion — the noun dīn (a complete system of belief, obedience, worship, and accountability to Allah) preceded by the preposition li- ('to/for'), expressing direction toward it or devotion for its sake.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the religion') governed by the preposition li- ('to/for'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which is required after a preposition. (The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following d, written as a doubled d.)

4.meaning: 'Upright in faith, naturally inclined to pure monotheism' — one who turns away from all false worship toward sincere devotion to the one Allah; a term for steadfast, primordial monotheistic faith.
4.grammar: A singular indefinite noun/adjective (an intensive 'faʿīl' pattern). The -an ending is accusative plus nunation: it marks indefiniteness ('a/an') and the accusative case, the form used for an object, a descriptive term, or a circumstantial state ('… as one upright in faith').
4.root: ح-ن-ف (ḥ-n-f) — to incline away (from error) toward pure monotheism

5.meaning: the nature / the innate disposition / the primordial constitution

parts.en: the natural disposition / primordial nature (construct, accusative)

5.grammar: noun, feminine, in construct state (iḍāfa), accusative — fiṭra means the innate natural disposition with which every human being is created; derived from faṭara 'to create, split, begin'; the -ta (tā marbūṭa) marks the feminine; in construct it requires no tanwīn; fiṭrat Allāh means 'the nature/constitution Allah has instilled'
5.root: ف-ط-ر (f-ṭ-r) — to create, originate, split; fiṭra: natural disposition

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
7.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

8.meaning: He originated / brought into being from nothing — to create by splitting open and fashioning anew, an act of fresh, foundational creation.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he…'), presenting the act as completed. With no added subject suffix, the doer is simply 'he.'
8.root: ف-ط-ر (f-ṭ-r) — to split open, originate, bring into being

9.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
9.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
9.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

10.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
10.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

11.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
11.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

12.meaning: Alteration or substitution — the act of changing one thing for another, replacing or modifying. The verbal noun names the process of exchange or transformation.
12.grammar: A masculine verbal noun of form II. The -a ending marks the accusative case, which commonly marks the object of a verb and is also the form used after the absolute-negation particle ('no change at all').

13.meaning: for the creation / in the creative act (of Allah)
