13.grammar: preposition + verbal noun in construct, genitive — li- expresses negation context (lā tabdīla li-khalqi Allāh: 'no change to Allah's creation'); khalq is in the genitive governed by li-; as a verbal noun it refers to the act of creation or to what has been created
13.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, fashion

14.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
14.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

15.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
15.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

16.meaning: A noun, 'the dīn.' Dīn spans religion, faith, the way of life one follows in obedience, and also judgement, reckoning, and recompense — the system of accountability and devotion one lives by and answers to.
16.grammar: A definite noun marked by al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or main topic of a sentence (the one doing or being something).

17.meaning: the correct / the upright / the straight (religion)
17.grammar: adjective (intensive pattern), definite, masculine singular, nominative — al-qayyim means 'the correct, upright, straight'; it is an intensive form indicating something that maintains correctness and is firmly established; the -u ending marks the nominative; used to describe the dīn al-qayyim 'the upright religion'
17.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand upright; qayyim: upright, correct

18.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
18.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

19.meaning: 'More' / 'greater (in number or amount)' — the comparative/superlative form built from 'much, many', meaning more numerous or more abundant.
19.grammar: A comparative adjective on the pattern afʿal ('more …'). The -a ending is the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is an object or otherwise governed; this pattern does not take nunation. It is typically completed by 'than …'.

20.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
20.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
20.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

21.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
21.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

parts.en: they know (3rd person masculine plural imperfect)

22.grammar: verb, active voice, imperfect tense (Form I), 3rd person masculine plural — the ya- prefix marks 3rd person; -ūna marks masculine plural indicative; ʿalima/yaʿlamu means 'to know, be aware of'; often used to conclude a statement about what people do or do not know

1.meaning: turning (to Allah) / returning (in repentance)
1.grammar: active participle (Form IV), masculine plural, accusative/genitive — munīb is one who turns back to Allah (from anāba 'to turn back, repent, return'); -īna marks the masculine plural accusative/genitive form; used as a circumstantial participle (ḥāl) meaning 'while turning back to Him'
1.root: ن-و-ب (n-w-b) — to return, alternate; Form IV: to turn back (to Allah)

2.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
2.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

3.meaning: 'And be mindful of Him / guard yourselves in awe of Him' — a command to have taqwā: a God-conscious reverence that makes one shield oneself from wrongdoing out of awe of Allah. With 'Him' attached as object. The root sense is to guard, shield, and protect oneself.

parts.en: verbal stem: be wary/mindful of, guard yourselves against (in reverent awe)

3.grammar: An imperative (command) verb of the iftaʿala pattern (which here conveys guarding oneself), addressed to a masculine plural audience by the -ū ending — 'you all.' The attached -hu is the object 'Him.' The whole conveys the command to hold protective, reverent God-consciousness toward Him.
3.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect; hence taqwā (reverent mindfulness)

4.meaning: And establish / set up / perform fully — a command to make something stand firm and upright, to carry it out properly and consistently (used especially of performing prayer rightly).
4.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') joined to a plural command verb of the causative (af'ala) pattern, meaning to make something stand/be upright. The -ū ending marks a masculine-plural addressee being told to do it.
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright; to establish

5.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
5.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.
5.root: ص-ل-و (ṣ-l-w) — prayer, worship, supplication

6.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: You (plural) are / you happen to be. A form of the 'hollow' verb kāna ('to be'), which links a subject to a state or description, or expresses simply being or existing.
7.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks 2nd person; the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The dropping of the usual final -na (so takūnū rather than takūnūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form expected after conditional or subordinating particles.
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

8.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
8.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

9.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
9.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.
9.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate, partner

1.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
1.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They split up / divided / separated (it)' — the past tense of a verb meaning to break something into parts, to cause division or to make distinctions/factions. The intensive form stresses a thorough splitting apart.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means the doers are 'they' (more than one male, or a mixed group). The doubled middle letter marks the intensive form, conveying a forceful or repeated splitting/dividing.

4.meaning: Their religion / way of life — the concept of dīn: the complete system of belief, worship, obligation, and obedience by which one lives and to which one is accountable; also rendered 'faith,' 'judgment,' or 'recompense' depending on context. Here joined to 'their.'

parts.en: religion, way of life, system of obedience and accountability

4.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hum ('their,' a group of men). The -a vowel before the pronoun reflects the accusative case — the form typically used when the noun is the direct object of a verb ('… their religion' as the thing acted upon).
4.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, obedience, judgment, requital, debt/accountability

5.meaning: A compound meaning 'and they were' or 'and they used to' — it sets a state or habit in the past. The verb 'to be/become' here establishes an ongoing past condition, often paired with a following verb to express habitual action.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb ('to be') in the third-person masculine plural — the -ū ending means 'they' did/were. It commonly conveys a continued past state or habit, especially when followed by another verb. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

6.meaning: Into factions, parties, sects — separate groups and partisan camps into which people split apart. An indefinite plural.
6.grammar: An indefinite broken plural noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, the case typically used for a direct object or to express the state/result into which something is brought ('… into factions').
6.root: ش-ي-ع (sh-y-ʿ) — to follow, to spread; faction, party

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'all, every, each, the whole of.' It expresses totality — when joined to a following noun it means 'every (one)' or 'the entirety of' that thing.
7.grammar: A noun of totality with the final -u ending (nominative). The -u typically marks it as the subject or the thing being spoken about. It normally attaches to a following noun to mean 'every / all of' it.

8.meaning: a party / a faction / a group
8.grammar: noun, masculine, indefinite, genitive — ḥizb means a group, faction, or party; the -in tanwīn marks it as indefinite and in the genitive; in Quranic usage it often describes a faction rejoicing in its own views (kull ḥizbin bimā ladayhim fariḥūn: 'each party rejoicing in what they have')

9.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
9.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
9.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

10.meaning: In their presence / with them / by them — an adverb of place meaning 'at/by/near', fused with 'them' (a group of males), indicating proximity or possession.

parts.en: at / with / in the presence of

10.grammar: The locational word ladā ('at / with / in the presence of'), which shifts to the form laday- when a pronoun is attached, here -him ('them', a group of males). It indicates nearness, presence, or possession.

11.meaning: An active participle (a doer-noun) meaning 'ones rejoicing / glad / exulting' — people filled with joy and delight, sometimes with the nuance of being elated or smug.
11.grammar: An active participle in the masculine plural, naming those in the described state: 'those who rejoice'. The -ūna ending marks the masculine plural in the nominative case, which is typically used for the subject or for a predicate describing the subject.
11.root: ف-ر-ح (f-r-ḥ) — joy, gladness, to rejoice

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: Touched, afflicted, or befell — for something (such as harm or hardship) to have made contact with someone.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he/it touched'). The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for a single masculine subject; the doubled middle consonant (shadda) is part of this root's basic form.
2.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch, make contact, afflict

3.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
3.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

4.meaning: hardship / harm / distress
4.grammar: noun, masculine, indefinite, nominative — ḍurr means harm, affliction, or hardship (the opposite of khayr 'good/benefit'); the -un tanwīn marks it as indefinite nominative; used for any kind of physical or material harm or distress that Allah tests or removes

5.meaning: 'They called upon / invoked / supplicated' — a past-tense verb meaning a group summoned, prayed to, or claimed something. The root spans calling out, naming, and inviting.
5.grammar: Past/perfect verb. The ending is wāw al-jamāʿa (the plural wāw, -aw), which marks a completed action by a third-person masculine-plural subject: 'they did [it].' The wāw is followed by a conventional silent alif (alif al-fāriqa), a purely orthographic spelling marker after this verbal plural ending — it is not pronounced and is unrelated to the sound-masculine-plural noun ending.
5.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, supplicate, invite.

6.meaning: Their Lord, Master, and Sustainer — 'rabb' is the one who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached pronoun, the Lord who is theirs.
6.grammar: A masculine noun with the possessive 'their' attached. The -a vowel before -hum marks the accusative case, the case typically used for the object of a verb.

7.meaning: turning (to Him) / returning in repentance
7.grammar: active participle (Form IV), masculine plural, accusative/genitive — same form as id 261 (munībīna); one who turns back to Allah in repentance; used as a circumstantial participle here as well; the doubled mīm (indicated by shaddah) is due to the preceding word ending
7.root: ن-و-ب (n-w-b) — to return; Form IV: to turn back to Allah

8.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

9.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
9.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

10.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
10.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

11.meaning: He caused them to taste / He made them experience

parts.en: He caused to taste (Form IV past tense)

11.grammar: verb (Form IV, past tense) + object pronoun — adhāqa is Form IV of dhāqa 'to taste'; Form IV (adhāqa) means 'to cause to taste, to let experience'; the subject is Allah; -hum is the 3rd person masculine plural object; used for both pleasant and unpleasant experiences
11.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste; Form IV: to cause to taste, let experience

12.meaning: A prepositional phrase, 'from him/it' — indicating origin or source, that something proceeds out of him/it.
12.grammar: The preposition min ('from') with the attached pronoun -hu ('him/it', third-person masculine singular). As the object of a preposition the pronoun stands in the genitive; the combination indicates source or origin.

13.meaning: Mercy: compassion that actively does good — tenderness joined with the will and power to relieve, forgive, and benefit. As a noun it names an instance or measure of such mercy.
13.grammar: An indefinite noun with the -an (accusative) ending, marked by tanwīn (the doubled-n sound). The accusative generally signals the word is a direct object or otherwise governed; the tanwīn marks it as indefinite — 'a mercy', 'some mercy'.
13.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

14.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
14.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

15.meaning: A group, party, or faction — a portion or section of people set apart from a larger body.
15.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The '-un' (tanwīn) marks it indefinite ('a group') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence.
15.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, divide; a division

16.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
16.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

17.meaning: 'In/with their Lord' — combining the preposition 'bi' (with, in, by) and 'rabb', meaning the Lord, Master, Nurturer, and Sustainer who owns, governs, and brings to maturity all that He has created; with the attached pronoun 'their'.
17.grammar: A preposition 'bi-' attached to the noun 'rabb', which then carries the possessive pronoun '-him' ('their'). Because it follows the preposition, the noun takes the genitive '-i' vowel (heard in 'rabbi'); after a word ending in '-i', the pronoun is voiced 'him' rather than 'hum'.
17.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain, and lord over

18.meaning: 'They associate (partners with Him)' — an ongoing/present verb. From the root for partnership, this form (causative, Form IV) means to make something a partner or associate, especially to set up partners alongside Allah in worship or divinity (the act underlying shirk).
18.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' doing the action now or habitually. The yu- prefix is the marker of Form IV (causative): 'to make (something) a partner.' The full -ūna ending signals the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state, not cut short by a governing particle.
18.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner; (causative) to associate partners

1.meaning: So that they may deny, reject, or be ungrateful — to cover over a truth or a favour and refuse to acknowledge it.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb after the particle 'li-' ('so that, in order to'), which puts it in the subjunctive of purpose. The 'ya-' prefix marks third-person, and the '-ū' ending marks a masculine-plural subject ('they'); the final 'n' that the plural would otherwise carry drops because of the particle.
1.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, deny, be ungrateful

2.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
2.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
2.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

3.meaning: We gave them / We granted them; a completed act of bestowing or providing, done by a "we" subject and directed to a group as recipients.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb meaning "to give/grant." The attached -nā marks the subject as "we" (the doer), and the attached -hum marks "them" as the recipients/object. The form states a completed action.
3.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (in this form) to bring, give, grant

4.meaning: then enjoy / so take pleasure (for a time)
4.grammar: particle + imperative verb (Form V), 2nd person masculine plural — tamattaʿū is the imperative of tamattaʿa 'to enjoy, take pleasure'; Form V adds reflexivity; the imperative here is often a threatening or concessive command ('enjoy while you can'); -ū marks the plural
4.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — to enjoy, benefit from; Form V: to take pleasure

5.meaning: A two-part marker meaning 'then/so' plus 'shall/will.' It announces something forthcoming as a consequence: the particle sawfa points to the future, generally a more remote or emphatic future than the shorter prefix sa-.
5.grammar: A linking particle fa- ('then/so,' signalling result or sequence) joined to the future particle sawfa, which is placed before a present-tense verb to throw its action into the future ('will/shall …').

6.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
6.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

2.meaning: We sent down — to cause something to descend or be revealed from a higher source to a lower; classically used of revelation sent down from on high.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb of the causative (fourth) form, meaning to make something come down. The attached -nā is the subject pronoun 'we', marking the action as completed and done by a 'we' (a form of majestic/collective speech when used of Allah).
2.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, be sent down

3.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
3.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
3.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: Authority, sanction, or compelling proof — power or warrant given to back something up, whether kingly authority or a decisive argument. 'Sulṭān' is authorizing power or evidence.
4.grammar: A single noun ('authority') carrying the accusative indefinite ending -an (tanwīn al-naṣb). This one ending does two things at once: the -a marks the accusative case (typically the direct object of a verb), and the final -n sound (nunation) shows the noun is indefinite ('an authority / any warrant'). The nunation is a diacritic on the case vowel, not a separable suffix, so the word stays one undivided token.

5.meaning: A two-part phrase: the connector 'then / so' plus the standalone pronoun 'he / it,' used to point back and resume with 'then he…' or 'so it…'
5.grammar: The connector 'fa' ('then/so') plus the detached subject pronoun 'huwa' ('he/it'), 3rd-person masculine singular. Both are indeclinable, with no case ending; the pronoun typically begins or emphasizes a statement about 'he/it.'

6.meaning: speaks / can speak / will speak

parts.en: he speaks / is able to speak (Form V imperfect)

6.grammar: verb, active voice, imperfect tense (Form V), 3rd person masculine singular — from takallama 'to speak'; Form V is the reflexive of kallama 'to address/speak to'; the -u ending marks the indicative; in Quranic contexts often used in the negative (lā yatakallamūna: 'they will not speak')
6.root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m) — to speak, address; kalima: word

7.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
7.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

8.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
8.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

9.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
9.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

10.meaning: 'They associate (partners with Him)' — an ongoing/present verb. From the root for partnership, this form (causative, Form IV) means to make something a partner or associate, especially to set up partners alongside Allah in worship or divinity (the act underlying shirk).
10.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' doing the action now or habitually. The yu- prefix is the marker of Form IV (causative): 'to make (something) a partner.' The full -ūna ending signals the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state, not cut short by a governing particle.
10.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner; (causative) to associate partners

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: 'We made (someone) taste / We caused to experience' — to let a person undergo or feel something (often a hardship or a favor), spoken in the first-person plural.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) causative verb (form IV — 'to make taste'). The suffix -nā marks the first-person plural ('we') as the doers and indicates a completed action. The causative form turns 'to taste' into 'to make someone taste / cause to experience'.
2.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste, to experience, to feel

3.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
3.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

4.meaning: Mercy: compassion that actively does good — tenderness joined with the will and power to relieve, forgive, and benefit. As a noun it names an instance or measure of such mercy.
4.grammar: An indefinite noun with the -an (accusative) ending, marked by tanwīn (the doubled-n sound). The accusative generally signals the word is a direct object or otherwise governed; the tanwīn marks it as indefinite — 'a mercy', 'some mercy'.

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'they rejoiced, became glad, or exulted.' The root conveys joy and delight, and at times an excessive, self-satisfied gladness.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending -ū marks a completed action by 'they' (masculine plural). The silent 'alif' written after the -ū is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.
5.root: ف-ر-ح (f-r-ḥ) — joy, gladness, exultation

6.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
6.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

7.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
7.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

8.meaning: Verb meaning 'it strikes / befalls / hits (them)' — to reach and affect someone, said of anything that lands upon a person, whether benefit or harm.

parts.en: strike, befall, hit the mark (hollow-verb stem)

8.grammar: A present-tense Form I verb of the hollow root ص-و-ب, with a feminine third-person subject ('she/it'), here in the jussive mood — the shortened form (note the bare '-ṣib' without a final vowel, the long vowel of the stem dropped) used after conditional particles ('if … strikes them') and certain other particles. The 'tu-' prefix is simply the Form I imperfect prefix for a feminine subject, not a Form IV marker. The attached '-hum' is the object 'them.'
8.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, strike correctly; to befall or reach

9.meaning: "A bad thing / an evil / a misfortune" — something evil, harmful, or unpleasant; a misdeed or a piece of bad fortune.
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun/adjective. The -at ending marks it feminine; the final -un is nominative case with tanwīn (the -n marking it indefinite, 'a bad thing'). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence. It is the counterpart of ḥasana.
9.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — evil, harm, to be bad

10.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
10.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

11.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she/it put forward / sent ahead / advanced beforehand' — to send something on ahead, often used of deeds a person has done in advance and dispatched before themselves.
11.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in an intensive pattern (doubled middle letter) that conveys deliberately putting something forward. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject, 'she' or 'it (feminine)', so it reads 'she/it sent ahead'.
11.root: ق-د-م (q-d-m) — coming before, advancing, putting forward

12.meaning: Their hands. The plural noun 'hands' carrying the masculine plural possessive 'their'; often used idiomatically for what people do, produce, or are responsible for through their own deeds.
12.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-him' meaning 'their' (a group of males, or mixed). 'aydī' is the irregular ('broken') plural of 'yad' (hand). The pronoun ending makes the whole construction definite and possessed; the 'i'-coloured stem before the suffix reflects its genitive/possessed state, the form typically following a preposition or standing as object.

13.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
13.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.
13.root: — (a time particle; no triliteral root)

14.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
14.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

15.meaning: they despair / they lose hope

parts.en: they despair / lose hope (3rd person masculine plural imperfect)

15.grammar: verb, active voice, imperfect tense (Form I), 3rd person masculine plural — from qanaṭa 'to despair, lose hope'; the ya- prefix marks 3rd person; -ūna marks masculine plural indicative; opposite of rajāʾ (hope); qunūṭ is the state of utter hopelessness
15.root: ق-ن-ط (q-n-ṭ) — to despair, lose hope completely

1.meaning: A compound opening a question and a negation at once: roughly 'and have … not …?' or 'is it not the case that …?'. It combines a questioning particle, the connector 'and', and a negative that places the following verb in the past, often expecting the listener to agree.
1.grammar: Three particles fused together: the interrogative 'a-' (turning the statement into a question), the connector 'wa' ('and'), and the negator 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and shifts its meaning into the past ('has not / did not'), and it puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (vowel-less) form. The combination often invites the listener to affirm ('have you not …?').

2.meaning: To see, perceive, or behold — and, by extension, to realize, observe, or come to recognize. The bare form here is the 'cut-short' (jussive) shape used after certain particles, so it reads 'they (do not) see'.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in its shortened (jussive) form, used after particles such as those that negate the past or express purpose/condition. The third-person masculine plural subject 'they' here takes the distinct jussive plural ending '-aw' (written wāw + a silent 'alif al-fāriqa). This '-aw' is the jussive paradigm's own ending in its own right, not the indicative '-ūna' with the 'na' stripped off.
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, behold

3.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
3.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
4.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

5.meaning: He spreads out, extends, stretches forth, and makes ample. The verb conveys laying something open and wide, and so giving abundantly or enlarging a provision.
5.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular; the 'ya-' prefix marks 'he/it', and the final '-u' marks the plain indicative — an ongoing or habitual action ('he extends / keeps extending'). The root pictures spreading a thing out flat and wide, hence giving generously.
5.root: ب-س-ط (b-s-ṭ) — spreading out, extending, expanding, making ample

6.meaning: The provision; sustenance, livelihood, and the means of life — whatever bounty is granted to support and nourish a creature, whether food, wealth, or any good thing bestowed.
6.grammar: A definite singular noun (the 'al-' prefix means 'the'; its 'r' doubles the sun-letter assimilation of the 'l'). It is a verbal noun on the 'fiʿl' pattern denoting that which is provided. The final '-a' is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing given or acted upon).
6.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — provision, sustenance, bestowing the means of life

7.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
7.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

8.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
8.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
8.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

9.meaning: And He measures out, restricts, straitens, or apportions sparingly; to set a fixed measure to provision so as to limit it. The same verb can also mean to have power and to determine.
9.grammar: The prefix 'wa' means 'and'. The core is a present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular; 'ya-' marks 'he/it', and the final '-u' marks the plain indicative — an ongoing or habitual action ('he restricts / keeps measuring out'). The root joins the ideas of measuring, decreeing, and having power.
9.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — measuring, apportioning, determining, power

10.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
10.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
11.root: — (particle)

12.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
12.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

13.meaning: Surely signs, tokens, or clear indications; evidences that point to a greater truth. The prefixed lām adds emphasis ('surely / indeed').
13.grammar: An emphatic particle 'la-' ('surely') joined to an indefinite feminine plural noun ('signs'). The -āt- is the sound feminine plural marker; the final -in (nunation) marks it indefinite. For this plural pattern the -in form serves for both the accusative and the genitive case.
13.root: ا-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token

14.meaning: For a people, for a folk or community; a group of human beings considered together. Joined to the preposition 'li' ('for / to').
14.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for / to') plus an indefinite singular noun ('a people'). The -in ending (nunation) marks indefiniteness; it is the genitive form, required because nouns governed by 'li' stand in the genitive.
14.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

15.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'they believe / they have faith' — to trust and affirm with the heart, to hold something true and place one's security in it.
15.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb built on the form IV pattern, which here functions intransitively, 'to have faith / to believe' (not a causative making someone else believe). The yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they.' The full -ūna ending (indicative mood) presents the action as ongoing or habitual fact: 'they (do) believe.'

1.meaning: so give / so bestow (to relatives/kin)
1.grammar: connective particle + imperative verb (Form IV), 2nd person masculine singular — āti is the imperative of ātā 'to give, bring'; the base imperative of Form IV ātā drops the hamza; the command is to give what is due to relatives, the poor, and travelers
1.root: أ-ت-و/ي (ʾ-t-w/y) — to come, bring; Form IV: to give

2.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'this one' or 'the one' — a pointing word ('that/this') used to single out a person or thing. It often combines with the question particle to form 'who is it that…?'
2.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this/that one'). It does not take case endings; the final -ā is part of the fixed word. It functions to point out or identify someone or something.

3.meaning: Nearness, kinship, closeness of relation — the bond of being near in blood, hence 'relatives' or 'near kin'. The word names the quality of family closeness itself.
3.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' (the). It ends in a fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra) that does not change for case; such words show their grammatical role through context rather than a changing final vowel. The sense is abstract: 'nearness of kin'.
3.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — to be near, close; nearness, kinship

4.meaning: Its rightful due, the obligatory claim or right that belongs to it. The stem ḥaqq denotes truth, rightness, and a binding entitlement that someone or something is genuinely owed.
4.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hu' meaning 'its' or 'his'. The base carries an accusative '-a' vowel, which typically marks a word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon), here joined to a possessor.
4.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, a binding entitlement or due

5.meaning: Means 'and the poor/needy one' — a person in want and destitution who lacks sufficient means. The term names someone reduced to neediness and humility.

parts.en: accusative ending (-a vowel on the final letter)

5.grammar: A definite singular noun prefixed with wa- ('and') and the article al- ('the'). It is a singular noun: the final nun is the last root letter of the word, and the accusative (object) state is marked only by the short -a vowel (fatha) on that nun. The word denotes one stricken by poverty and need.
5.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — stillness, being subdued (poverty that subdues a person)

6.meaning: 'And the son of' — 'son', the first part of a fixed expression (ibn al-sabīl, 'son of the road' = the traveller/wayfarer). Joined by 'and'.
6.grammar: The connector wa ('and') plus the noun 'son'. It begins with a hamzat al-waṣl (a helping vowel 'i-' that is dropped in connected speech). The final -a is the accusative case; as the first term of a possessive phrase it must be followed by another noun ('son OF …').
6.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w / b-n-y) — son, offspring; building up

7.meaning: The way, road, or path — a route one travels; very often used figuratively for a course of life, conduct, or the path of religion. The attached article makes it definite: 'the way'.
7.grammar: al- is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates to the following 's', heard as 'as-sabīl'). The final -i is the genitive ending, marking the word as joined to a preceding noun ('… OF the way') or governed by a preposition.

8.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
8.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

9.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
9.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
9.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

10.meaning: 'For/to those who …' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the masculine plural relative pronoun 'those who,' which introduces a description of a group by something they do.
10.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to') fused with the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). Relative pronouns like this do not change for case; they point ahead to a clause that describes the group ('those who …').

11.meaning: they want / they intend — to will, desire, or purpose something. The verb conveys an active, ongoing intention or wish on the part of a group.
11.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb (arāda, 'to will/intend'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the ending -ūna marks masculine plural plus the indicative mood (a plain statement: 'they want'). The -na would drop under a particle that changes the mood.
11.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, will, intend

12.meaning: Face — literally the front of the head; figuratively the foremost part, the outset, or the direction one turns toward.
12.grammar: A singular noun. The '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or signals an adverbial sense such as time or manner.
12.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, front, direction one turns to

13.meaning: The proper name of the One True God in Arabic — Allah, the unique, supreme Deity worshipped alone, without partner or equal. It is a name, not a common noun, and is not pluralized or made feminine.
13.grammar: The divine proper name. The final '-i' (kasra) is the genitive case — the case taken after a preposition or when the name is linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah'). Being a name, it carries no indefinite tanwīn.
13.root: — (the divine proper name; not derived from a triliteral root in the ordinary sense)

14.meaning: 'And those' — the connective 'and' joined to the demonstrative 'those'. It both links to what precedes and points out a group ('and it is those who…').
14.grammar: A connecting particle wa ('and') prefixed to a plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. The wa simply joins what follows to what came before. The demonstrative is fixed in form (no case endings), and its -ka element marks distance; it may refer to people of either gender.

15.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
15.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

16.meaning: 'The successful / the ones who flourish' — those who attain what they seek and are saved from what they fear. The underlying sense is of prospering, thriving, and winning through to lasting wellbeing and salvation, not merely worldly success.
16.grammar: A definite active participle (Form IV) in the masculine plural: 'the ones who succeed/prosper'. The al- prefix makes it definite ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate identifying who someone is.

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) gave' or 'you brought/handed over' — a completed act of giving or bestowing something, performed by a group being addressed.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with the ending -tum, meaning 'you all' did it — the subject is a group being addressed. The completed (perfect) form indicates a finished act of giving. The long ā at the start belongs to the causative pattern, which gives the sense 'to make (something) come (to someone)', i.e. to give or hand over.
2.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to bring, to give

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

4.meaning: usury / interest / an increase on a loan
4.grammar: noun, masculine, indefinite, accusative — ribā means any increase or excess in an exchange, specifically usurious interest; the -an tanwīn marks it as indefinite accusative; the doubled rāʾ is a spelling convention; ribā is prohibited in Islamic law
4.root: ر-ب-و (r-b-w) — to increase, grow, be more

5.meaning: so that it may increase / in order that it grows

parts.en: so that / in order to (lam of purpose)

5.grammar: lam of purpose + verb in subjunctive (Form I), 3rd person masculine singular — li- introduces the purpose clause; yarbuwā is the subjunctive form of rabā 'to increase, grow'; the weak wāw ending in the subjunctive; refers to the mistaken belief that giving ribā causes wealth to increase with Allah
5.root: ر-ب-و (r-b-w) — to increase, grow, be more

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

7.meaning: Possessions / wealth; the property and goods belonging to people.
7.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, masculine. The -i ending marks the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun in an 'of'-relationship.

8.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
8.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
8.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

9.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
9.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

10.meaning: it increases / it grows (in return)

parts.en: it increases / grows (3rd person singular imperfect)

10.grammar: verb, active voice, imperfect tense (Form I), 3rd person masculine singular — the indicative form (with -ū written for the weak wāw) of rabā 'to increase, grow'; refers to how zakāh given for Allah's sake actually multiplies in reward, contrasted with ribā
10.root: ر-ب-و (r-b-w) — to increase, grow, be more

11.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
11.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').
11.root: — (adverb of place)

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
13.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
13.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

The long ā at the start belongs to the causative pattern, which gives the sense 'to make (something) come (to someone)', i.e. to give or hand over.
14.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to bring, to give

15.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
15.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

16.meaning: zakah / purifying alms / obligatory charity
16.grammar: noun, feminine, indefinite, genitive — zakāh is the obligatory annual alms-giving in Islam, one of its five pillars; derived from zakā 'to be pure, to grow'; the -tin tanwīn marks it as indefinite genitive; the root meaning combines purity and growth — giving purifies wealth and causes blessings to multiply
16.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure, to grow; zakāh: purifying charity

17.meaning: You (plural) want, intend, desire, or seek — to direct one's will toward something and aim at it.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb in the 'you all' form. The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject and signals the causative (form-IV) pattern; the suffix -ūna combines the masculine-plural subject ('you all') with the indicative mood — the kept final -na shows a plain statement (not a command or subjunctive, where that -na would drop).
17.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to go to and fro after something; will, intention

18.meaning: Face — literally the front of the head; figuratively the foremost part, the outset, or the direction one turns toward.
18.grammar: A singular noun. The '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or signals an adverbial sense such as time or manner.
18.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, front, direction one turns to

19.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
19.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

20.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
20.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

21.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
21.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

22.meaning: those who receive manifold increase / those whose giving is multiplied

parts.en: those who multiply / get manifold increase (masculine plural nominative)

22.grammar: definite active participle (Form IV), masculine plural, nominative — muḍʿif is Form IV active participle of ḍāʿafa 'to double/multiply'; the -ūna ending marks masculine plural nominative; refers to those whose good deeds are multiplied by Allah, specifically those who give zakāh sincerely
22.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — to double, multiply; Form IV: to cause multiplication

1.meaning: Allah — the proper name of the One God, the sole and absolute Deity worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a name, not a common noun, and refers to the Creator and Sustainer of all that exists.
1.grammar: The proper divine name. The final -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject (the doer) of a sentence or the noun being identified.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: 'He created you' — He brought you into existence, originating and shaping you. The verb denotes bringing something into being and giving it its form and proportion, here with 'you (plural)' as the one(s) created.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb with an attached object pronoun. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer in the completed past ('he created'). The suffix '-kum' is the object 'you (plural),' i.e. the ones to whom the action was done.

4.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
4.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

5.meaning: He provided for you / He gave you sustenance
5.grammar: verb (past tense, Form I) + object pronoun — razaqa is 3rd person masculine singular past tense of razaqa 'to provide sustenance'; the subject is Allah; -kum is the 2nd person masculine plural object pronoun; rizq (provision) encompasses all forms of sustenance Allah provides
5.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide, sustain; rizq: provision, sustenance

6.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
6.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

7.meaning: 'He causes (someone) to die' — a causative verb from the root meaning death: to bring about death, to make a living thing die. The causative form turns 'to die' into 'to put to death / to cause to die'.
7.grammar: Present/future tense. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') in the causative (form IV) pattern; the bare unending imperfect signals ongoing or future action ('he will / does cause to die'). The attached -kum is a plural object pronoun, 'you (all)'.

8.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
8.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

9.meaning: 'He gives life' or 'He brings to life' — a causative verb from the root meaning life: to make alive, to revive, to grant living existence to what was lifeless.
9.grammar: Present/future tense. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') in the causative (form IV) pattern; the imperfect without a jussive/subjunctive ending expresses ongoing or future action ('he gives / will give life'). The attached -kum is a plural object pronoun, 'you (all)'.
9.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life, living

10.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
10.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
11.root: — (preposition)

12.meaning: 'Your partners' — those whom a group sets up as associates or co-sharers, especially partners associated with Allah in worship (idols or false deities). The base noun denotes a partner, associate, or sharer in something.
12.grammar: A plural noun with the attached possessive pronoun -kum meaning 'your' (addressing a group of males or a mixed group). The -i case-vowel before the pronoun is genitive, the case typically used after prepositions or when a word is possessed/linked to what precedes.
12.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate, take as a partner

13.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
13.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

14.meaning: A verb meaning 'he does / he acts / he carries out' — to perform or bring about an action.
14.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he' subject. The final -u marks the indicative mood, indicating an ongoing, habitual, or general action ('he does / keeps doing').

15.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
15.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

16.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
16.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

17.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
17.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

18.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
18.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
18.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

19.meaning: An exclamation of glorification meaning 'far removed and utterly above all imperfection is He.' The verbal noun 'subḥān' declares that the One referred to is exalted beyond any deficiency, partner, or fault, and the attached 'Him' directs that declaration to a single masculine being.
19.grammar: A verbal noun used as an absolute exclamation, fixed in the accusative ending -a (an emphatic declaration, roughly 'I declare His utter transcendence'). The attached -hu is the possessive/object pronoun 'Him', referring to one masculine person.
19.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide away, hence to declare Allah free of all imperfection

20.meaning: 'And He is exalted/transcendent high above' — to be far above and beyond, used of Allah being utterly lofty and removed from any deficiency or false attribution.
20.grammar: wa is 'and'. taʿālā is a past-tense verb (form VI) functioning as an exclamation of glorification; its final long -ā marks third-person masculine singular ('He'). The form intensifies the root sense to 'be supremely high, transcendent'.
20.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — to be high, lofty, exalted

21.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
21.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

22.meaning: they associate (partners with Allah) / they commit shirk

parts.en: they associate partners / commit shirk (3rd person masculine plural imperfect)

22.grammar: verb, active voice, imperfect tense (Form IV), 3rd person masculine plural — from ashrika 'to associate, make a partner'; Form IV (ashrakabihi) means to associate something with Allah, i.e., commit shirk (polytheism); -ūna marks masculine plural indicative
22.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate; Form IV: to commit shirk/polytheism

1.meaning: It became apparent, visible, or open; it came out into the open. The verb means to show or manifest plainly, and can also carry the sense of being outward or external as opposed to hidden.
1.grammar: A past-tense (completed action) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The 3ms past form carries no overt subject suffix; the final fatḥa is the inherent vowel of the verb's own pattern, not a subject-marking ending. It presents the becoming-apparent as something that has happened.
1.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — to appear, become manifest, be outward

2.meaning: the corruption / the corruption (on land and sea)
2.grammar: definite noun, masculine, nominative — al-fasād means corruption, destruction, or disorder in the moral, social, or ecological sense; the -u ending marks the nominative; fasād is the result of human transgression and wrongdoing
2.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — to corrupt, spoil, go wrong; fasād: corruption

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The dry land — solid ground as opposed to the sea; the terrain one travels on foot.
4.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition or when the word is linked to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship. The doubled r (shadda) is part of the stem.

5.meaning: 'And the sea' — 'baḥr' is the sea or any large body of water; by extension a vast expanse. Made definite as 'the sea'.
5.grammar: A definite noun with the '-i' ending, which marks the genitive case — the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). Prefixed 'wa' means 'and'.
5.root: ب-ح-ر (b-ḥ-r) — sea, vast body of water

6.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
6.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

7.meaning: 'It earned / acquired, gained' — said of deeds and their consequences; the root means to gain or acquire something, especially the moral 'earnings' of one's actions.
7.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it.' The past tense presents the action as completed.
7.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

8.meaning: the hands / what their hands have done
8.grammar: broken plural noun, in construct (iḍāfa) — aydī is the broken plural of yad 'hand'; in construct before a possessive pronoun (mā kasabat aydī al-nās 'what the hands of people have earned'); the final yāʾ is the construct ending; 'hands' here idiomatically means what one has done or earned

9.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
9.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
9.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

10.meaning: so that He may let them taste / so that He causes them to experience

parts.en: He lets taste / causes to taste (Form IV subjunctive)

10.grammar: lam of purpose + Form IV subjunctive + object pronoun — li- introduces the purpose; yudhīqa is the subjunctive of adhāqa (Form IV of dhāqa); the subject is Allah; -hum is the object; the purpose is that people experience consequences of their own deeds
10.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste; Form IV: to let taste, cause to experience

11.meaning: a part of / some of / a portion of — a noun denoting a piece or fraction of a larger whole (in the accusative form).
11.grammar: A noun meaning 'part' or 'some'. The final -a ending is accusative, marking it as a direct object or, with a measure of time, an adverbial span. It is normally followed by a noun in the genitive ('part of …').
11.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, a portion, some

12.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
12.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

13.meaning: They did / they worked — to perform a deed or action, to do work. The base word covers purposeful action and labor.
13.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The -ū ending marks 'they' (a group of males) as the doers (the silent alif after it is a spelling convention).
13.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, act, work, perform a deed

14.meaning: 'So that they may / perhaps they will.' A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose, fused with the pronoun 'them'; it introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

14.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps, in the hope that, so that') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), which serves as its subject. Laʿalla belongs to a family of particles that put a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -hum is that fixed object form. It conveys hope or an intended purpose rather than certainty.

15.meaning: To return, go back, or turn back — to come back to a place, state, or point of origin. Used of a group: 'they return / come back'.
15.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they return'). The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks an ongoing or repeated action by a group of males or a mixed group. The -ūna 'indicative' ending appears when nothing precedes the verb to shorten it.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.
