2.meaning: A command addressed to a group of males (or a mixed group): 'travel!', 'journey!', 'move through the land!'. It urges people to set out and move across the earth, often with the sense of journeying so as to observe and reflect.
2.grammar: Command (imperative) verb. The -ū ending marks a command given to more than one male person, i.e. 'all of you, travel!'. The stem comes from a hollow root, so the original middle letter appears here as a long ī.
2.root: س-ي-ر (s-y-r) — to travel, journey, move along

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
4.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

5.meaning: So look! / observe! — a command to a group to look, gaze, and consider; to direct one's sight and attention so as to see and reflect. The opening 'so/then' links the command to what precedes.
5.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group, prefixed with fa- ('so/then'). The -ū ending aims the order at a masculine plural 'you' ('you all, look!'). The initial helping vowel (u-) appears because the bare stem would otherwise begin with two consonants together.
5.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, see, observe, consider

6.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
6.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

7.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

7.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

8.meaning: The outcome, end-result, or final consequence — what a matter or a course of conduct ultimately comes to. It names the end that follows from a beginning.
8.grammar: A feminine noun. The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or, without nunation as here, the first term of a possessive phrase ('the outcome of …'). It denotes that which comes at the heel — the consequence that follows on.
8.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow, come after (at the heel); an end, consequence

9.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
9.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
11.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
11.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

12.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

12.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

13.meaning: Most of them / the greater part of them — the noun 'akthar' (the greater number, the majority), built on a comparative/superlative pattern of k-th-r ('much/many'), with the pronoun 'them'.
13.grammar: A noun in possessive (genitive) construction: 'aktharu' ('the most of') plus the attached pronoun '-hum' ('them') yields 'most of them'. The '-u' on 'akthar' is the nominative ending, typical when this phrase serves as the subject.
13.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, numerous

14.meaning: polytheists / those who associate partners (with Allah)
14.grammar: active participle (Form IV), masculine plural, accusative/genitive — mushrik is one who commits shirk (associating partners with Allah); the -īna ending marks the masculine plural accusative/genitive (oblique case); mushrikūn (nominative) / mushrikīna (oblique)
14.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to associate; mushrik: one who associates partners with Allah

1.meaning: so set / so establish / so direct (your face)
1.grammar: connective particle + imperative verb (Form IV), 2nd person masculine singular — fa- introduces the consequential command; aqim is the imperative of aqāma (Form IV of qāma) 'to establish, set upright'; when used with wajhaka ('your face') it means to set/direct oneself firmly
1.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand; Form IV: to establish, set upright

2.meaning: Your face; the front of the head — and by extension one's countenance or direction. Addressed to a single male ('your'), and here the object of an action.
2.grammar: The noun 'face' (wajh) with the attached pronoun -ka ('your', for one male). The -a ending before the pronoun is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('turn … your face').
2.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, that which one faces

3.meaning: To / for the religion — the noun dīn (a complete system of belief, obedience, worship, and accountability to Allah) preceded by the preposition li- ('to/for'), expressing direction toward it or devotion for its sake.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the religion') governed by the preposition li- ('to/for'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which is required after a preposition. (The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following d, written as a doubled d.)

4.meaning: the correct / the right / the upright (religion)
4.grammar: definite adjective (intensive form), genitive — al-qayyim in the genitive (governed by a preposition or in construct); same root and meaning as id 259 (al-qayyim nominative); the genitive -i marks its grammatical position; refers to the upright, straight religion or way
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand; qayyim: upright, correct, maintaining

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'before' — denoting that which precedes in time or order.
6.grammar: An adverb/noun of time. The -i ending is genitive, which here arises because it follows a preposition (commonly 'min', 'from'); it characteristically links to a following noun ('before … OF …').
6.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; the front or prior side

7.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
7.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

8.meaning: '(that) it comes' or 'so that it may come' — to arrive, come, or approach. The verb denotes something drawing near or coming to pass.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The final -a (subjunctive) ending, rather than the usual -u, signals that the verb is governed by a preceding particle such as 'that' or 'before/until' — giving the sense 'that it come' or 'so that it may come.'

9.meaning: 'a day' — a period of daylight, a single day, or more broadly an appointed time or epoch. It can refer to an ordinary day or to a momentous, decisive day.
9.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -un ending is nominative and indefinite ('a day'): the doubled-n (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite, and the -u vowel typically marks it as the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.
9.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, time

10.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
10.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

11.meaning: A noun meaning 'a turning back, a repelling, a reversal' — the act or possibility of something being averted or sent back; also 'no averting it' when negated.
11.grammar: A verbal noun of place/action (the ma- prefix forms such nouns) meaning 'a turning back / averting.' The final -a ending is accusative; this is the form a noun takes as a direct object, and notably the form used after the absolute negation particle ('there is no … at all').
11.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — returning, sending back, repelling

12.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
12.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

13.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
13.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

14.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
14.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

15.meaning: On that day / that day — pointing back to a particular past day already in view; 'a day, at that time.'
15.grammar: A time-word ('day') joined to 'idhin' ('at that time'), together meaning 'on that day.' The '-in' ('tanwīn') compensates for an understood clause ('the day when…'). The form functions adverbially, locating an event at a specific past moment.

16.meaning: they will be divided / they will split apart (at the Hour)

parts.en: they will be divided / shattered (3rd masculine plural imperfect)

16.grammar: verb, imperfect tense (Form V/VI intensive), 3rd person masculine plural — the original Form V of ṣadaʿa 'to crack, split'; with assimilation the ya- and ta- merge; -ūna marks masculine plural indicative; the word describes shattering or dividing into fragments, like a cracked vessel
16.root: ص-د-ع (ṣ-d-ʿ) — to crack, split, shatter; Form V: to split apart

1.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
1.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

2.meaning: He disbelieved / rejected — to refuse faith, deny the truth, and turn away ungratefully from Allah. The root also carries the sense of covering over or being ungrateful for a blessing.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he disbelieved'). The final -a ending marks completed past action done by a single male. The verb denotes rejecting faith and being ungrateful, covering over the truth.
2.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, reject faith, be ungrateful

3.meaning: 'Then upon Him / so on Him' — the preposition 'upon/on' with the pronoun 'him', preceded by 'then/so', conveying that something rests upon or is directed onto him.
3.grammar: A connective 'fa-' ('then / so', often showing result) with the preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon'), whose form shifts to 'ʿalay-' when a pronoun is attached. The pronoun takes the -hi form (rather than -hu) because it follows the 'ay' sound. Placing this phrase first typically gives a sense of 'upon Him [alone] …'.

4.meaning: his disbelief / his rejection (falls on himself)
4.grammar: verbal noun in construct + possessive pronoun — kufr is the verbal noun/noun from kafara 'to disbelieve, cover/conceal'; the -u marks the nominative (as subject); -hu is the 3rd person masculine singular possessive; together: 'his disbelief' — indicating the consequences of disbelief fall on the person themselves
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; kufr: disbelief, rejection

5.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
5.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
5.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

6.meaning: 'He did / worked / acted' — to perform a deed or action, to do work.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base form. With no added subject-suffix and the final -a, it carries the default third-person masculine singular subject, 'he did'. The past tense presents the action as completed.

7.meaning: righteous (deeds) / good (work)
7.grammar: adjective or active participle (Form I), masculine singular, indefinite, accusative — ṣāliḥ means righteous, sound, good (of deeds or people); the -an tanwīn marks indefinite accusative; often used in 'ʿamila ṣāliḥan' (did righteous deeds); ṣāliḥ describes what is morally sound and pleasing to Allah
7.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, righteous, good; ṣāliḥ: righteous

8.meaning: then for themselves / then it is for their own benefit
8.grammar: connective + preposition + noun in construct + possessive — fa- links to preceding; li- indicates benefaction; anfusi is the construct genitive of anfus (plural of nafs); -him is the possessive; together: 'then it is for their own selves' (i.e., righteous deeds benefit the doer)
8.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul; nafs singular, anfus plural

9.meaning: they are preparing / they are making ready (their abode)

parts.en: they prepare / make smooth (3rd masculine plural imperfect)

9.grammar: verb, active voice, imperfect tense (Form I), 3rd person masculine plural — from mahada 'to smooth out, prepare, make a bed'; -ūna marks masculine plural indicative; figuratively means to prepare or pave the way for oneself (like preparing a bed or dwelling for their own future)
9.root: م-ه-د (m-h-d) — to smooth, prepare; mahd: cradle, prepared place

1.meaning: '...so that He may reward/requite' — to give due recompense, repaying a person according to their deeds, whether good or ill.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he requites'), preceded by 'li-' meaning 'so that / in order that', which expresses purpose. Because of this particle the verb takes the subjunctive mood, shown by the final '-a' (here '-ya' on the weak-ending verb) instead of the usual '-u' — marking an intended or hoped-for outcome rather than a plain fact. It typically takes an object: the one being recompensed.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
4.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

5.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
5.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
5.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: 'His bounty / grace / favor' — faḍl is overflowing generosity, an extra goodness given beyond what is owed; with the attached pronoun it means the bounty belonging to Him (Allah).
7.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the noun to what follows in an 'of' relationship; here it carries through to the possessor.
7.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus; hence bounty, grace, superiority

8.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
8.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

9.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

10.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
10.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

11.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
11.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
11.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

1.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
1.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

2.meaning: 'His signs / His verses.' The plural of a word meaning a sign, token, or mark that points to a greater reality — also used for the verses of revelation — here joined to 'his'.
2.grammar: A sound feminine plural ('signs') with an attached possessive 'his'. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form this plural takes when it follows a preposition or is linked as the object of a possessor; the -hi ('his') marks ownership: 'his signs'.
2.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark; a verse of revelation

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: 'That He should send / let loose.' The verb means to send forth, dispatch, or release something so that it goes out toward a target — a messenger, wind, rain, or punishment.

parts.en: (that) he — yu- prefix doubled by assimilation of a preceding 'an'

4.grammar: A present-tense Form IV (causative) verb in the subjunctive. The imperfect prefix 'yu-' marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), and the Form IV shape is seen in the stem 'yu-rsil-' (perfect 'arsala'). It is written with a shadda ('yyu-') because a preceding particle 'an' ('that') loses its final 'n', which assimilates (idghām) into the 'y': 'an yu-' becomes 'a-yyu-'. The final '-a' is the subjunctive ending required after that particle, giving 'that he should send'.
4.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a messenger, that which is sent

5.meaning: the winds / the breezes
5.grammar: definite noun, feminine plural, accusative — al-riyāḥ is the broken plural of rīḥ 'wind'; the -a ending marks the accusative (object of a verb); in Arabic, riyāḥ (plural) often carries positive connotations (winds of mercy), while rīḥ (singular) can denote a destructive wind
5.root: ر-و-ح (r-w-ḥ) — wind, breath, spirit; riyāḥ: winds

6.meaning: bearers of good news / announcers of glad tidings

parts.en: bringers of glad tidings (feminine plural indefinite genitive)

6.grammar: active participle (Form II), feminine plural, indefinite, genitive — mubashirāt is the feminine plural of mubashshir 'one who brings good news' (Form II active participle); the -in tanwīn marks indefinite genitive; in feminine plural because it describes the winds (riyāḥ), which are grammatically feminine
6.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — good news, skin; Form II: to announce good news

7.meaning: and to let you taste / and so He causes you to experience

parts.en: so that / in order to (lam of purpose)

7.grammar: conjunction + lam of purpose + Form IV subjunctive + object pronoun — wa- is connective; li- introduces the purpose clause; yudhīqa is the subjunctive of adhāqa (Form IV: to cause to taste); -kum is the 2nd person masculine plural object; Allah causes people to experience His mercy through the winds and rain
7.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste; Form IV: to let taste

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

9.meaning: Mercy, compassion, tender care that actively benefits its object — joined to 'His': His mercy.
9.grammar: A feminine noun joined to the attached pronoun -hi ('his / its'). The -i vowel on the stem is the genitive ending, which appears because the noun is linked to a following possessor or follows a preposition ('... of ...'); the -hi suffix names that possessor: 'His mercy.' The original feminine -t- sound surfaces because a suffix follows.
9.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, loving care

10.meaning: and so that may sail / and that (the ships) may run

parts.en: it runs / sails (3rd feminine singular subjunctive)

10.grammar: conjunction + lam of purpose + verb (Form I) in subjunctive, 3rd person feminine singular — li- introduces purpose; tajriya is the subjunctive of jarat 'to run, flow, sail'; 3rd person feminine (agreeing with al-fulk 'ships', which can be feminine); the purpose of the winds also includes enabling maritime travel

11.meaning: the ships / the vessel(s)
11.grammar: noun, definite, nominative — al-fulk is remarkable in Arabic for being both singular and plural (like English 'sheep'); the -u ending marks the nominative; it can refer to a single ship or to ships collectively; used in Quranic contexts for the ships that sail the seas by Allah's permission
11.root: ف-ل-ك (f-l-k) — ship, orbit, celestial sphere

12.meaning: With/by His command — amr means a command, order, decree, or matter/affair; with the preposition bi- ('with, by') and the pronoun 'His' it conveys 'by His command' or 'by His decree'.
12.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with' or 'by'. The noun amr takes the genitive -i ending (required after the preposition bi-) and then the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The genitive marks the noun as governed by the preposition.
12.root: ء-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command, order; a matter/affair

13.meaning: 'And so that you may seek / desire' — to strive after and pursue something, to seek to obtain a benefit or bounty. The Form VIII verb conveys earnest seeking.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb in Form VIII (to seek, desire) with 'and' plus the purpose-particle 'so that'. The ta- prefix means 'you'; the -ū ending (nūn dropped) marks plural 'you all' in the subjunctive of intent ('so that you may seek').
13.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after

14.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
14.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

15.meaning: 'His bounty / grace / favor' — faḍl is overflowing generosity, an extra goodness given beyond what is owed; with the attached pronoun it means the bounty belonging to Him (Allah).
15.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the noun to what follows in an 'of' relationship; here it carries through to the possessor.
15.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus; hence bounty, grace, superiority

16.meaning: And so that you (plural) may; in the hope that you might. The particle laʿalla expresses hope, expectation, or a desired outcome ('perhaps / so that'), here with 'you' as its subject.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in the hope that

16.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps / in hope that'), which expresses an anticipated or hoped-for result, with the attached pronoun -kum ('you all') as its subject. Such particles place the following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -kum here is that subject. It typically leads into a verb stating the hoped outcome. The wa- ('and') links it to what comes before.

17.meaning: 'You (all) give thanks / are grateful'. To recognize a kindness and acknowledge it — with the heart, tongue, and deeds — toward the one who bestowed it.
17.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix signals a 'you' subject, and the '-ūna' ending marks a plural masculine 'you' in the ongoing (indicative) mood — 'you all give thanks'. The retained '-na' shows the verb stands free of any negating or governing particle.

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: We sent / dispatched. From the causative verb meaning to send forth or commission, especially the sending of messengers; with 'We' as the subject.
2.grammar: Past/perfect verb in the causative (form IV) pattern meaning 'to send', 1st person plural ('we'). The suffix -nā is the subject ending 'we' on a completed action. The perfect tense presents the sending as accomplished and complete.
2.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching, messengership

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: 'Before you' (in time or place): the period or position prior to a single person — that which comes earlier or stands in front, relative to one addressee.
4.grammar: The adverb/noun qabl ('before, prior') with the attached pronoun -ka ('you', a single male). The -i ending on qabl is genitive, the case regularly taken after a preposition (such as min, 'from before') and when a noun is linked to a following possessor; here it is linked to the pronoun 'you' ('before-you').
4.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, be before; priority, what comes first

5.meaning: 'messengers' — envoys, those sent by Allah bearing a message to people.
5.grammar: The broken (irregular) plural of rasūl ('messenger'). The -an ending is accusative with tanwīn, typically marking the word as a direct object and indefinite ('messengers').
5.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; messenger, message

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
6.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

7.meaning: Their people — the folk, nation, or community to which they belong; one's own kin and tribe. 'Qawm' denotes a body of people bound together as a group.
7.grammar: A singular collective noun with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' ending is genitive — the form a noun takes after a preposition, or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of their people').
7.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — standing, rising; a people who stand together

8.meaning: So they came to them — a past-tense act of a group arriving at or coming up to another group, whether approaching, reaching, or confronting them.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb prefixed with 'fa' ('so/then'). The '-ū' ending means 'they' (a group) did it, and the attached '-hum' is the object ('… them'), giving 'so they came to them'.

9.meaning: 'With the clear proofs / evident signs' — bayyināt are plain, self-evident demonstrations that make the truth manifest, leaving no doubt.
9.grammar: Built from 'bi-' ('with/by means of') + 'al-' ('the') + a feminine plural noun meaning 'clear proofs.' The -i ending is the genitive case, required after the preposition 'bi-'; the feminine sound plural '-āt' takes -i (not -a) in this case. The whole phrase means 'with the clear proofs.'
9.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, distinctness, making plain

10.meaning: 'So we took retribution / we exacted justice.' The verb means to avenge, to punish in just recompense, to exact a penalty for a wrong. It carries the sense of a measured, deserved requital rather than random anger.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb in the reflexive/intensive (Form VIII) pattern, in the 'we' person, with a connective prefix. The fa- means 'so / then,' marking a consequence. The stem intaqam- is completed (past) action. The -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers ('we exacted retribution'). The Form VIII pattern (with the infixed -t-) gives the sense of taking the act fully upon oneself.
10.root: ن-ق-م (n-q-m) — to avenge, exact retribution, punish a wrong

11.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
11.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

12.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
12.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

13.meaning: 'They committed crimes / they sinned.' Past-tense from 'ajrama' (Form IV), to perpetrate a crime, sin, or guilt-bearing wrong. Refers to a group having done such deeds.
13.grammar: Past-tense Form IV verb. The '-ū' ending (with a silent spelling-alif) marks a completed action done by 'they' (masculine plural). Past-tense verbs encode their subject in the ending rather than a prefix: here, a plural 'they'.
13.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to commit a crime or sin; guilt, wrongdoing

14.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

15.meaning: A right, a due, or an obligation — that which is true, real, and rightfully owed; an established duty. As an adverbial accusative it conveys "as a duty/obligation, in truth, bindingly."
15.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The '-an' (nunation on the fatḥa, with a following alif) often functions adverbially here — "as a binding duty" or "in truth" — describing the manner or affirming the statement.
15.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, right, established; truth, right

16.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
16.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

17.meaning: Help, aid, victory, or succour — divine or human assistance that brings relief and triumph against an adversary.
17.grammar: A masculine verbal noun. The final -u is the nominative ending, generally marking the word as the subject of a sentence or as the thing being described.
17.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to aid, to grant victory

18.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
18.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

1.meaning: Allah — the proper name of the One God, the sole and absolute Deity worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a name, not a common noun, and refers to the Creator and Sustainer of all that exists.
1.grammar: The proper divine name. The final -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject (the doer) of a sentence or the noun being identified.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: He sends, sends forth, dispatches, or lets loose. An ongoing/repeated action of releasing or sending something on its way.
3.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third person masculine singular ("he …"), of the causative form ("to send forth, dispatch"). The yu- prefix marks "he" plus this verb pattern; the final -u marks the plain indicative (a simple statement of fact).
3.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send, dispatch; messenger, message

4.meaning: The winds — moving currents of air. A plural noun denoting winds, often associated with bringing rain and mercy.
4.grammar: A definite plural noun. The -a ending is accusative, which generally marks the word as the object of a verb (the thing being acted upon). The "l" of "al-" assimilates into the following "r" (al-riyāḥ → ar-riyāḥ).
4.root: ر-و-ح (r-w-ḥ) — wind, breath, spirit; rest, relief

5.meaning: so they raise / so they stir up (clouds)

parts.en: they stir up / raise (3rd feminine singular imperfect)

5.grammar: result particle + verb (Form IV, imperfect), 3rd person feminine singular — fa- indicates the result of the winds being sent; tuthīru is Form IV of thāra 'to be stirred up'; the feminine singular agrees with riyāḥ (winds, treated as a group); the winds stir up the clouds
5.root: ث-و-ر (th-w-r) — to stir up, rouse; Form IV: to cause to rise

6.meaning: Cloud, or a mass/collection of clouds; the gathered vapor that carries rain. A collective noun for cloud-matter.
6.grammar: An indefinite collective noun in the accusative case. The -an (tanwīn) marks it indefinite ("a cloud / clouds") and accusative, a case that generally marks the object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
6.root: س-ح-ب (s-ḥ-b) — to drag, draw along; cloud (drawn across the sky)

7.meaning: then He spreads it / then He stretches it out (the clouds)
7.grammar: sequence particle + verb (Form I, imperfect, 3rd masculine singular) + object pronoun — fa- marks sequence; yabsuṭu is from basaṭa 'to spread out, extend'; -hu refers to the cloud (saḥāb, masculine); Allah spreads out the clouds after the winds gather them
7.root: ب-س-ط (b-s-ṭ) — to spread out, extend; basṭ: extension

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
9.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
9.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; sky, heaven

10.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
10.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

11.meaning: "He wills / wishes / desires" — denotes an act of will or volition, the choosing of something. As an ongoing/present-tense verb it expresses willing as a continuous, sovereign act.
11.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the 'he' form. The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain, ongoing statement of fact ('he wills').
11.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish

12.meaning: and He makes it / and He turns it (into something)
12.grammar: conjunction + verb (Form I, imperfect, 3rd masculine singular) + object pronoun — yajʿalu from jaʿala 'to make, turn, place'; -hu is the object pronoun referring to the cloud; jaʿala with two objects means 'to make something into something' (He makes it layered/stacked)

13.meaning: Fragments, pieces, or broken-off portions; chunks of something split apart (such as a sky broken into segments).
13.grammar: A plural noun meaning 'pieces/fragments'. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('pieces'), commonly marking the object of a verb or describing the state in which something is ('in pieces').
13.root: ك-س-ف (k-s-f) — to cut off, break into pieces; eclipse

14.meaning: And you see, you behold, you observe. The verb covers both physical sight and the wider sense of perceiving or coming to realise something.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male ('you see'), preceded by the connective fa- ('so, then'). The ta- prefix marks the second-person addressee. The verb ends in a weak final letter (the -ā sound), and in its base indicative form it states an ongoing act of seeing.

15.meaning: the rain / the drops of rain
15.grammar: definite noun, masculine, accusative — al-wadq means rain or raindrops; the -a ending marks the accusative (as the object of yakhruju 'comes out'); a less common word for rain compared to maṭar, specifically denoting the drops that emerge from clouds

16.meaning: It comes out, emerges, or goes forth — the act of issuing or sprouting out from a source, said of one masculine subject in the present/ongoing sense.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb for a single masculine subject ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine; the final -u ending is the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact about an ongoing or habitual action (as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form).

17.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
17.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

18.meaning: their midst / within it / through its gaps
18.grammar: noun in construct state (iḍāfa), genitive + possessive pronoun — khilāl means the space between things, or midst; the -i marks the construct genitive; -hi is the 3rd person masculine singular possessive referring to the cloud (saḥāb); together: 'through its midst' (rain falling from within the cloud)
18.root: خ-ل-ل (kh-l-l) — midst, between, gap; khilāl: within, through

19.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
19.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.

20.meaning: 'It struck / befell / afflicted' — a past-tense verb describing something (often a punishment or hardship) reaching and hitting its target.
20.grammar: A past-tense Form IV verb in the third-person masculine singular ('it/he …'). The final -a is the standard third-person masculine singular past ending, stating that the action 'struck/befell' has occurred.
20.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, befall, afflict

21.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
21.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

22.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
22.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

23.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
23.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
23.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

24.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
24.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

25.meaning: 'His servants / His slaves / His worshippers' — ʿibād are those who serve and worship; with the attached pronoun it denotes the servants belonging to Him (Allah), i.e., humankind or His devotees.
25.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel is the genitive case, typically appearing after a preposition or in a possessive ('of') link; the pronoun names the one to whom the servants belong.

26.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
26.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

27.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
27.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

28.meaning: A verb meaning 'they receive glad tidings / rejoice at good news', and in this intensive (derived) form 'they eagerly welcome and delight in good news'. The face brightens at the arrival of something good.
28.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood — a plain statement that this is happening.

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
2.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'before' — denoting that which precedes in time or order.
4.grammar: An adverb/noun of time. The -i ending is genitive, which here arises because it follows a preposition (commonly 'min', 'from'); it characteristically links to a following noun ('before … OF …').
4.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; the front or prior side

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
5.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
5.root: — (particle; no root)

6.meaning: That it be sent down / caused to descend — the bringing down of something (such as revelation or a blessing) from above, in an intensive 'sent down (in stages/abundantly)' sense.
6.grammar: Present-tense passive verb ('it is sent down'), third-person masculine singular, in an intensive pattern (form II) suggesting sending down gradually or abundantly. The yu- prefix with the inner vowels marks the passive ('is being…'); the doubled (shaddah) yā reflects assimilation of a preceding sound into it in connected speech. The final -a ending is the subjunctive mood, the form taken after particles meaning 'that / so that / not'.

7.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
7.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
7.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

9.meaning: Before; the period or point in time (or place) prior to something. With the attached pronoun it means 'before it / before him', pointing to what came earlier.
9.grammar: An adverb/noun of time meaning 'before', functioning here as something governed in the genitive (the -i ending), as it regularly follows a preposition such as 'from'. The attached -hi means 'it / him' ('before it'); the vowel of the pronoun is -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows the -i ending.
9.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede; front, priorness

10.meaning: surely in despair / certainly hopeless
10.grammar: emphatic lam + active participle (Form IV), masculine plural, accusative/genitive — la- is the lam of emphasis; mublisīna is the plural of mublis 'one who despairs'; Form IV (ablasa) means 'to despair, be struck dumb with despair'; the -īna ending marks the masculine plural oblique; used when people see no rain after drought
10.root: ب-ل-س (b-l-s) — to despair; Form IV: to be in utter despair

1.meaning: So look! / then observe! — a command to one person to look at, consider, and reflect upon something.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you', prefixed by fa- ('so/then'), which links it as a consequence of what precedes. The verb urges one to look and reflect: 'so look!' / 'then consider!'
1.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, see, observe, consider

2.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
2.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

3.meaning: the effects / the traces / the signs
3.grammar: broken plural noun, genitive — āthār is the broken plural of athar 'trace, effect, sign'; the -i ending marks the genitive (governed by a preposition or in construct); refers to the traces or effects of something previously existing, such as the effects of Allah's mercy

4.meaning: Mercy, compassion, loving-kindness; tender care that moves one to relieve and benefit another. As a verbal noun it names the quality and act of showing mercy.
4.grammar: A feminine verbal noun (the tāʾ shows as 't' when joined to what follows). The final -i is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a following noun ('mercy OF …') or follows a preposition. Being genitive, it is the possessed/linked term in such a construction.

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
6.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

7.meaning: 'He gives life / brings to life / revives.' The act of granting life or restoring it to the lifeless, attributed to a single male/divine subject.
7.grammar: A present/imperfect-tense verb on the causative pattern ('to cause to live'). The yu- prefix marks the subject as 'he'. The stem comes from a root whose last two letters are both yāʾ; the final yāʾ is written once and is part of the root itself, not a separable ending. It means 'he gives life / revives'.
7.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life, to live; (causative) to give life

8.meaning: 'the earth,' 'the ground,' 'the land' — the earth as a whole, or the land/ground beneath us. It denotes the terrestrial expanse on which creatures live and walk.
8.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case) — the role of the thing acted upon, e.g. the direct object of a verb. The prefixed 'al-' makes it definite, 'the earth.'

9.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
9.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
9.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

10.meaning: Its death, its lifelessness or dormancy; the state of being dead, joined to a possessor.
10.grammar: A noun ('death') with an attached third-person feminine singular possessive pronoun ('its / her'). The -i vowel on the noun is genitive, the case taken before a possessor pronoun and after prepositions ('death of it').

11.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
11.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

12.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
12.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

13.meaning: surely He will give life / He certainly gives life

parts.en: the life-giver / one who gives life (active participle, construct)

13.grammar: emphatic lam + active participle (Form IV) in construct — la- is emphatic; muḥyī is the active participle of aḥyā 'to give life'; in construct before a genitive it means 'the giver of life to...'; the ending is in the construct (no case vowel visible); one of Allah's attributes
13.root: ح-ي-و/ي (ḥ-y-w/y) — life; Form IV: to give life, revive

14.meaning: 'The dead' — those who have died or are without life; the lifeless, as a group.
14.grammar: A definite plural noun/adjective ('the dead'). It is of a plural pattern that ends in a fixed long -ā, so its ending does not change with grammatical position; it refers collectively to those who are dead.

15.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
15.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

16.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
16.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

17.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
17.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

18.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
18.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
18.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

19.meaning: All-powerful, fully able, ever-capable — possessing complete and effective power to do whatever is willed; one whose ability never falls short.
19.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses a deep, abiding quality ('thoroughly able'). The final -un is the indefinite nominative (nunation) — the doubled-n shows no 'the', and the -u base vowel marks the nominative case, used when the word is a subject or a predicate ('… is all-powerful').

1.meaning: A combination meaning 'and surely if' — introducing a hypothetical condition ('if…') sworn by an implied oath, so that the outcome is strongly anticipated; roughly 'and by all means, if…'.
1.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb, so it takes no case ending: wa- 'and', the lam al-qasam (the 'lam of swearing') that marks the following condition as sworn by an implied oath, and in 'if' which sets up the condition. This oath-lam construction correlates with a later response clause that itself carries emphasis (an emphatic lam plus the 'nūn of emphasis' on its verb), giving the sense 'and [I swear] if … they would surely …'.

2.meaning: We sent / dispatched. From the causative verb meaning to send forth or commission, especially the sending of messengers; with 'We' as the subject.
2.grammar: Past/perfect verb in the causative (form IV) pattern meaning 'to send', 1st person plural ('we'). The suffix -nā is the subject ending 'we' on a completed action. The perfect tense presents the sending as accomplished and complete.
2.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching, messengership

3.meaning: a wind / a (dry, blighting) wind
3.grammar: noun, feminine, indefinite, accusative — rīḥ (singular) used here for a specific wind, contrasted with the life-giving plural riyāḥ; the -an tanwīn marks it as indefinite and accusative; a single wind can be a sign of destruction or hardship (as when it turns the crops yellow)
3.root: ر-و-ح (r-w-ḥ) — wind, breath; rīḥ: a wind

4.meaning: and they see it / and they behold it
4.grammar: particle + verb (past tense, Form I, 3rd masculine plural) + object pronoun — fa- is connective; raʾaw is 3rd person masculine plural past tense of raʾā 'to see'; -hu is the object pronoun; refers to people seeing the crop or the vegetation turn yellow due to the blighting wind

5.meaning: turn yellow / yellowed
5.grammar: passive participle (Form IX type / Form II), masculine singular, indefinite, accusative — muṣfarr comes from iṣfarra (Form IX) meaning 'to become yellow'; the Form IX (iCCaCCa) pattern is used for colors and defects; the -an tanwīn marks it as indefinite accusative (describing the yellowed state of vegetation)
5.root: ص-ف-ر (ṣ-f-r) — yellow; iṣfarra: to become yellow

6.meaning: they would certainly remain / they certainly continue (to disbelieve)
6.grammar: emphatic lam + verb (past tense, Form I), 3rd person masculine plural — la- is the lam of emphasis used with oaths; ẓalla/yaẓallu means 'to remain, continue in a state'; -ū marks the masculine plural past tense; together: 'they would certainly continue (in disbelief)' — showing the ingratitude of human nature
6.root: ظ-ل-ل (ẓ-l-l) — to remain, continue to be; related to shadow

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

8.meaning: 'After him / it' — 'baʿd' denotes what comes afterward in time or sequence, here joined to 'him/it'.
8.grammar: A time-noun 'baʿd' (afterness) with an attached pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. The '-i' vowel on 'baʿd' is its case ending, set by 'baʿd's' own position in the sentence (commonly governed by a preceding preposition), not by the suffix; the attached '-hi' is the possessor ('him/it'), and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive. The pronoun's 'i'-vowel (-hi rather than -hu) follows because it comes after a genitive '-i'.

9.meaning: 'They disbelieve / reject faith', or more literally 'they cover over (the truth), they are ungrateful'. An ongoing or habitual rejection and denial.
9.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a masculine plural 'they' acting now or habitually; the final -na (kept, not dropped) shows the verb is in its plain indicative form, stating an ongoing fact.
9.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — covering over; hence disbelief and ingratitude

1.meaning: A two-part opener meaning roughly 'then/so, truly You …': a connecting 'then/so' joined to an emphatic particle that asserts what follows with certainty, plus an attached 'You.' The emphatic particle (inna) strongly affirms the statement, like saying 'indeed' or 'it is certainly the case that.'
1.grammar: A particle cluster, not a verb. fa- is a connector ('then, so, and thus'). inna is an emphatic/affirming particle that places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative; here that pronoun is the attached -ka ('you,' one male), the topic being emphasized. There is no tense or case ending of its own.

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: To make someone hear, to convey sound to another's ears — and by extension to make a message reach and register with someone, to get through to them.
3.grammar: Present-tense verb of the causative (form IV) pattern, 'to make hear'. The tu- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'), and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain, ongoing or general action ('you make [someone] hear').

4.meaning: 'The dead' — those who have died or are without life; the lifeless, as a group.
4.grammar: A definite plural noun/adjective ('the dead'). It is of a plural pattern that ends in a fixed long -ā, so its ending does not change with grammatical position; it refers collectively to those who are dead.

5.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
5.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

6.meaning: To make someone hear, to convey sound to another's ears — and by extension to make a message reach and register with someone, to get through to them.
6.grammar: Present-tense verb of the causative (form IV) pattern, 'to make hear'. The tu- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'), and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain, ongoing or general action ('you make [someone] hear').

7.meaning: Those who cannot hear — the deaf. Often used figuratively for people who refuse to listen to or heed the truth.
7.grammar: A plural noun/adjective with the definite article al- ('the'). The l of al- assimilates into the following ṣ (a 'sun letter'), so it is pronounced ṣ-ṣumma. The final -a is the accusative ending, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('the deaf ones' as the thing acted upon).

8.meaning: The call, the appeal, the summons — an act of calling out, invoking, or supplicating.
8.grammar: A definite noun. The -a ending is accusative, the case typically taken by the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The word covers both calling out to someone and prayerful invocation.
8.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, supplicate

9.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.
9.root: — (a time particle; no triliteral root)

10.meaning: They turned away, turned their backs, or went off in retreat; to wheel around and depart, often signalling rejection or withdrawal from something faced.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb in an intensive (form II) pattern, which adds force to the bare sense of 'turning.' The plural -ū ending (here written -aw because the verb's last root letter is weak) marks the doers as 'they' — a group of males who completed the action.
10.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to turn, be near, take charge / turn away

11.meaning: Turning one's back, going away, retreating; people in the act of departing. This is the masculine plural active participle of 'to turn away', in the accusative/genitive form, often describing the manner in which people leave.
11.grammar: Active participle of a Form IV verb (ʾafʿala), following the mufʿil participle pattern, sound masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the accusative or genitive of a masculine plural; as an accusative it commonly functions as a circumstantial description ('while turning away').
11.root: د-ب-ر (d-b-r) — the back, hind part; to turn the back, to go away

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
2.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

3.meaning: can guide / is a guide for

parts.en: one who guides / a guide (active participle, construct)

3.grammar: preposition + active participle (Form I) in construct — bi- is used with the negative (lā+verb+bi-hādi) to mean 'not a guide for'; hādi is the active participle of hadā 'to guide'; in construct before the genitive it means 'a guide for/of'; the phrase: 'you cannot guide the blind'
3.root: ه-د-و/ي (h-d-w/y) — to guide; hādi: a guide

4.meaning: the blind / those who are blind (in heart or sight)
4.grammar: definite broken plural noun, genitive — al-ʿumyī is the broken plural of aʿmā 'blind' (the elative/adjective pattern); the -i ending marks the genitive (object of a preposition or after a construct); in Quranic usage often refers to those who are spiritually blind, unable to perceive the truth
4.root: ع-م-و/ي (ʿ-m-w/y) — to be blind; aʿmā: blind; ʿumyī: the blind

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

5.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

6.meaning: their error / their misguidance
6.grammar: feminine noun in construct state (iḍāfa), genitive + possessive pronoun — ḍalāla is the verbal noun/noun of ḍalla 'to stray, go astray'; -ti marks the construct genitive (tā marbūṭa in construct); -him is the possessive; together: 'their straying/misguidance'
6.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray; ḍalāl: misguidance

7.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
7.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

8.meaning: To make someone hear, to convey sound to another's ears — and by extension to make a message reach and register with someone, to get through to them.
8.grammar: Present-tense verb of the causative (form IV) pattern, 'to make hear'. The tu- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'), and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain, ongoing or general action ('you make [someone] hear').

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
9.root: — (particle)

10.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
10.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

11.meaning: He believes, has faith, trusts securely — to affirm something as true with the heart and place trust in it; an ongoing or characteristic believing.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb in the (āmana) pattern. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine 'he/it' as the doer, and the final -u (unmarked here) indicates the ordinary, unconditioned present ('he believes / does believe').
11.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, faith

12.meaning: By/in Our signs. Āyāt is the plural of āya — a sign, token, or evidence. Signs are pointers that indicate a greater reality. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'with/in Our signs'.
12.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, in, by'), which requires the following noun to take the -i (genitive) ending. The attached -nā means 'our' when joined to a noun. The genitive here is governed by the preposition.

13.meaning: Means 'so they / then they' — the connector 'so/then' joined to the standalone pronoun 'they' (for a group of males or a mixed group). It draws a consequence and then names the subject.
13.grammar: The connecting particle fa- ('so/then', drawing a result or sequence from what precedes) attached to the detached subject pronoun hum ('they', masculine or mixed plural). As a standalone pronoun it has no case ending and serves as the subject of what follows.

14.meaning: Ones who submit — those who have surrendered themselves wholly to Allah; 'Muslims' in the literal sense of people in a state of submission and peace with their Lord. A plural describing the subject of a sentence.

parts.en: one who submits / surrenders to Allah

14.grammar: An active participle (form IV) meaning 'one who submits'. The -ūna ending marks the sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when the plural is the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing the subject.
14.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — to be safe/whole; (form IV) to surrender, submit
